## Problem

`shared/tree_coverage.py` `run_coverage_review` / `apply_coverage_review` compare a parent's acceptance criteria against the ACs of **every direct child**, including children auto-created by the `triage` skill from a boilerplate `[test-failure]` template ("the test passes on latest dev", "all related documentation is updated", "full project test suite passes").

When such a triage child is re-parented under the hardening item that actually owns the flake (the documented triage practice), the parent can never reach `stage: plan_complete`: the template ACs do not textually match the parent's ACs, so the review returns `recommendation: "stop"` and the plan skill is required to leave the item `open` without advancing the stage.

Observed on AH-0MVWCFS7K000RIWI (2026-10-31): coverage 0 %, three unresolved conflicts on AC1/AC2/AC4, both children the triage template (AH-0MVWNIP0G002ZHOU critical, AH-0MVWJOH9T0006R1E medium). The same shape will be hit by every hardening/flake item that acquires reparented triage children.

## Expected behaviour

The coverage gate should treat auto-generated triage children differently from plan-generated feature children — e.g. exclude children tagged `test-failure` (or otherwise identified as triage-generated) from AC-coverage comparison, or exclude closed children, or allow an explicit "coverage credit" declaration on the parent mapping a child to a parent AC.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A parent work item whose only children are triage-generated `[test-failure]` items can reach `stage: plan_complete` without the coverage review returning `stop`.
- AC2 — Genuine plan-generated feature children are still coverage-checked exactly as today (no weakening of the gate for real decompositions).
- AC3 — Unit tests in `skills/shared/tests` cover: triage-only children (proceed), mixed triage + feature children (feature children still evaluated), and closed children.
- AC4 — `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` (or the relevant plan/triage docs) records the rule and its rationale.

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MVWCFS7K000RIWI (plan run blocked by this gate)
- Evidence precedent: AH-0MVWDOOY6004HF4W closed as a duplicate of the same hardening item.

## Plan review (plan skill, auto-complete path)

Auto-complete path taken: effort **Extra Small** / risk **Low** (below the
autoplan threshold), so **no child features were created**. This item is a
single minimal end-to-end slice: helper change, unit tests, documentation note.

### Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — AC coverage review (`run_coverage_review`, `compute_coverage`, `resolve_coverage_gaps`, `apply_coverage_review`); the triage exemption belongs here.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — existing unit-test suite for the helper.
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — canonical triage child creation; sets `--tags test-failure`, `--issue-type bug`, `--stage intake_complete` (this is the marker an exemption can key on).
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — plan-skill implementation reference; record the rule and its rationale here.
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — plan-skill operational brief (AC coverage review step).
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — triage skill brief (re-parenting practice).

The helper, its tests and the referenced doc live in the **SorraAgents**
framework repo (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`), not
in the AI_Hell game repo.

### Implementation assumptions

- The exemption keys on the `test-failure` tag set by the triage script; the
  `[test-failure]` title prefix is not used as the primary signal.
- Exempt (triage-tagged) children are excluded from the AC comparison but stay
  visible in the review output (reported as excluded) so the audit trail is
  preserved; `coverage` is computed from the remaining children only.
- When every direct child is exempt, coverage is vacuously complete and the
  review recommends `proceed` (AC1).
- Tag-less children keep today's behaviour exactly (AC2): same Jaccard
  thresholds (0.4 coverage, 0.2 auto-close floor), same `stop` semantics.
- Test-first: write the three AC3 unit tests first (red), then implement the
  exemption (green).

### Verification

- AC1 — unit test with a stubbed `wl` runner whose only children carry `tags: ["test-failure"]`; assert `run_coverage_review` returns `recommendation: "proceed"` and `apply_coverage_review(target_stage="plan_complete")` advances the stage.
- AC2 — existing coverage tests keep asserting tag-less children are compared and still produce `stop` when their ACs do not match.
- AC3 — `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` gains the three cases: triage-only (proceed), mixed triage + feature (feature children still evaluated), closed children (documented behaviour per the OPEN QUESTION below).
- AC4 — `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` gains a section stating the rule, the `test-failure` marker and the rationale: re-parented triage children must not block `plan_complete`, while genuine decompositions stay gated.
- Suite run via `/skill:test` (never ad-hoc pytest).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer interview was conducted: this was a downtime-dispatched
auto-complete plan run (effort Extra Small / risk Low, below the planning
threshold), so the plan proceeded on the documented assumptions above.

- OPEN QUESTION (directed to Producer; non-blocking) — AC3 requires a unit test
  for "closed children" but does not state the expected outcome. Recommended
  default: a closed child is exempt **only** when it is also tagged
  `test-failure`; a closed tag-less feature child keeps taking part in the
  coverage comparison exactly as today (conservative — exempting all closed
  children would let a parent pass the gate by closing an uncovered feature
  child). The AC3 "closed children" test will assert this default explicitly,
  so a later decision is a one-line change. Why it matters: the alternative
  (exclude every closed child) weakens the gate for real decompositions.

### Plan changelog

- 2026-11-01 — plan skill (auto-complete path): added Key Files, implementation
  assumptions, verification map, Appendix and this changelog; no child items
  created (below planning threshold); stage advanced `intake_complete` →
  `plan_complete`.

## Goal

Measure where the frame time actually goes at 100 late-game enemies, record the current baseline, and turn the profile into a ranked, evidence-based optimisation backlog.

**User story:** As a developer, I want a CPU profile and a recorded baseline for the 100-enemy scenario, so I know which hot spots are worth fixing and in what order — instead of guessing.

## Why

The parent item is a **proactive** optimisation pass with **no existing profiling** (producer answers 1–2), and the brief's structural suspects (allocations, collision passes, per-frame `Graphics` redraws) are unmeasured. The parent's AC6 requires every optimisation to cite profiler evidence and before/after numbers. This child produces that evidence and sets priorities for the structural children.

## Scope

- Run the frame-time harness (sibling child) against `GymPerformance` (sibling child) and `PlayScene` late game.
- Capture a **CPU profile** via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`Profiler.start`/`Profiler.stop`) during a sustained 100-enemy run, on desktop browser and the packaged Electron app; under a CPU throttle for the mobile tier.
- Attribute frame time across coarse buckets: JS simulation (movement/fire/collision/drops), renderer draw submission, GC/allocation, audio, telemetry, idle.
- Record a **baseline table** in the work item and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`: per-bucket ms, p50/p95/max frame time, FPS, long-frame counts, platform, throttle factor, reference-machine description, commit hash.
- Produce a **ranked hotspot list** with source locations (`file:line`), each with measured share and an estimated win. File or update optimisation child items from that list and **set their priorities by measured impact** — including re-ranking the pre-created structural children (broad-phase collision, per-frame allocations, GPU offload/draw-call batching).
- Determine whether the loop is genuinely CPU-bound or renderer/GPU-bound, and state that conclusion explicitly (the parent's premise "assuming we are CPU bound" must be confirmed or refuted).

## Out of scope

- Implementing any optimisation (children created here do that).
- Changing gameplay behaviour, waves or balance.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A CPU profile for a sustained 100-enemy run is captured and stored/linked (artifact path recorded), on desktop browser and Electron, plus a CPU-throttled mobile-tier run.
2. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` contains the baseline table with p50/p95/max frame time, effective FPS, long-frame counts, per-bucket attribution, platform, throttle factor, reference-machine description and commit hash.
3. A ranked hotspot list with `file:line` locations and measured share of frame time is recorded as a comment on this item and in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
4. The CPU-bound vs renderer-bound question is answered with evidence, and the answer is recorded on the parent work item.
5. Optimisation child items exist for the measured hotspots (creating them if the pre-provisioned structural children do not cover a hotspot), each carrying its measured impact, and their `priority` values are set from that impact — not from speculation.
6. Re-running the harness after no code change reproduces the baseline within the harness noise floor, confirming the baseline is trustworthy.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- **Parent AC trace — parent AC3.** **Baseline recorded.** A baseline measurement from the current `main` is captured on desktop browser and Electron with the stress gym at 100 enemies, and the numbers are recorded in the work item and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. This baseline is the "before" number every optimisation child must beat. *(Traces to parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC3; this item is where it is satisfied.)*
- **Parent AC trace — parent AC6.** **Evidence-driven changes.** Every optimisation child records the profiler evidence (hotspot, share of frame time, source location) that justifies it and the before/after harness numbers. Hotspots found during profiling become child work items, prioritised by measured impact — not by speculation. *(Traces to parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC6; this item is where it is satisfied.)*

## Key files (predicted)

- `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` — harness (sibling child)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts` — stress scene (sibling child)

## Goal

Remove the super-linear collision work from the shared combat pass so cost scales with (n + m) rather than (n × m) at 100 enemies and their fire.

**User story:** As a player in the late game, I want collisions to stay cheap when hundreds of bullets and bodies are on screen, so frame time does not collapse as the screen fills.

## Why (structural suspect — re-rank on profiler evidence)

`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_handleCollisions` (~:1226) runs:
- player bullets × enemy bullets — a nested loop over every pair,
- enemy bullets × player — a full scan (fine),
- player bullets × enemies via `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`,
- player body × every enemy body.

At 100 enemies plus sustained fire, the bullet-vs-bullet pass is quadratic in bullet count. This is a **structural suspect**, not yet measured; the profiling child must confirm its share before this is prioritised up.

## Scope

- Introduce a broad-phase in the shared collision pass (uniform grid / spatial hash keyed by bullet and body cell) so bullet-vs-bullet and body-vs-body candidates are only tested within neighbouring cells.
- Keep the **exact same resolution semantics and ordering**: nearest/first-hit selection must produce identical outcomes to the current pass for the same inputs, so determinism and parity are preserved.
- Apply in the shared core only (`src/scenes/core/`), so gyms and `PlayScene` keep running the same code.
- Add a benchmark-style test asserting candidate-pair counts drop at high bullet densities, plus equivalence tests asserting identical collision outcomes against the current implementation on the same fixtures.

## Out of scope

- Changing hitboxes, damage, or gameplay balance.
- Per-frame allocation reduction in movement/fire collection (sibling child).
- Renderer/draw-call work (sibling child).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The broad-phase lives in `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by the shared collision pass; no scene keeps a divergent copy.
2. Collision outcomes are byte-for-byte identical to the pre-change implementation on a fixture set covering bullet-vs-bullet, bullet-vs-player, body-vs-body, Force Field reflect, AOE detonation and splitting projectiles (equivalence test proves it).
3. A test measures candidate-pair checks at a high density (e.g. 300 player bullets × 300 enemy bullets) and asserts a large reduction (target ≥ 10×) versus the naive nested loop.
4. Seeded determinism is unchanged: the same seed produces the same run outcome before and after.
5. The measured 100-enemy scenario shows a recorded improvement (before/after harness numbers on this item) or, if profiling shows the pass is not hot, the item is closed with that evidence and no code change.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_handleCollisions` (~:1226), `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `_overlaps`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — equivalence guard
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — bullet collections
- `src/utils/` — likely home for the new broad-phase helper
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — record the measured win

## Dependencies

Blocked by the profiling child (evidence + baseline) and the harness child.

## Goal

Eliminate the avoidable per-frame allocations in the hot loop so the GC does not punctuate the late game with collection pauses.

**User story:** As a player in the late game, I want a steady frame time without GC hitches, so the game does not stutter when the screen is busiest.

## Why (structural suspect — re-rank on profiler evidence)

The per-frame path allocates transient arrays and closures even when nothing changes:

- `PlayScene._collectEnemyFire` (~:4254) builds `this.spawned.filter(...).map(...)` for aim targets, then iterates `this.spawned` again pushing into `this.enemyBullets` with spread of a fresh array per enemy.
- `PlayScene._moveEnemies` (~:2708) builds `this.spawned.filter(...).map(...)` for seek targets every frame.
- `PlayScene.getEnemyEntities` (~:4322) does `this.spawned.map(s => s.entity)` on every collision pass.
- `CombatScene._handleCollisions` builds `keptEnemy` / `keptEnemy2` arrays each frame.

At 100 enemies this is thousands of short-lived objects per second. This is a **structural suspect**, not yet measured; the profiling child must confirm GC share before reprioritising.

## Scope

- Replace per-frame `filter().map()` / spread-into-array patterns with reused scratch buffers or in-place iteration that preserves ordering exactly.
- Reuse the collision `kept*` buffers across frames (clear + push), keeping resolution order identical.
- Ensure the shared helpers (`pushAimTargets`, `pushSeekTargets`, `advanceWrappingBullets`, `advancePlayerBullets`) keep their current signatures or gain allocation-free variants without forking behaviour between gyms and the game.
- Add allocation-counting tests (e.g. instrumenting array creation via a counter seam, or asserting scratch-buffer identity reuse) so the property is guarded.

## Out of scope

- Broad-phase collision (sibling child).
- Renderer/draw-call work (sibling child).
- Any gameplay change.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_collectEnemyFire` performs no per-frame array allocation for aim targets or the fire-collection accumulator, verified by a test (reused buffer identity / allocation counter).
2. `_moveEnemies` seek-target push and `getEnemyEntities` use pre-allocated or cached collections, verified by tests.
3. The collision pass reuses its `keptEnemy`/`keptEnemy2` buffers across frames, with a test asserting buffer reuse and unchanged ordering.
4. No behaviour change: existing parity/equivalence suites pass, and a seeded run produces identical outcomes before and after.
5. The measured 100-enemy scenario shows a recorded GC-time and frame-time improvement (before/after harness numbers on this item), or the item is closed with profiler evidence that the allocations are not material.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_collectEnemyFire` (~:4254), `_moveEnemies` (~:2708), `getEnemyEntities` (~:4322)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_handleCollisions` (~:1226)
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts` (or wherever `pushAimTargets`/`pushSeekTargets` live)
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — record the measured win

## Dependencies

Blocked by the profiling child (evidence + baseline) and the harness child.

## Goal

Cut per-frame draw-submission and CPU→GPU work where the profiler shows it dominates, by caching static `Graphics` into textures and using batched/particle paths for repeated primitives.

**User story:** As a desktop player, I want the renderer to spend its time drawing enemies and action rather than re-issuing the same HUD and bubble geometry every frame, so the 60 FPS target holds at 100 enemies.

## Why (structural suspect — re-rank on profiler evidence)

Several pieces of chrome are cleared and re-drawn from scratch on every frame:

- `CombatCoreScene._updateOptionsEscort` (~:1292) calls `graphics.clear()`, `lineStyle`, `strokeCircle`, `fillStyle`, `fillCircle` per pod per frame.
- Shield bubble, Force Field bubble and Thorns aura graphics are redrawn each visual update (`PlayScene.ts` ~:1279–1286 creation; redraw in the visual update path).
- The wave timer bar calls `g.clear()` + `fillRect` every frame (`PlayScene.ts` ~:4985–4997).
- HUD `refresh()` runs on every tick (`src/scenes/core/hudWiring.ts`).

Additionally, the parent brief asks for **GPU offload where we are CPU-bound** (producer, item description). The profiling child will determine whether the win is draw-call batching (static geometry → `RenderTexture`/cached texture, or a single batched `Graphics` re-drawn only on change) or sprite/particle batching for repeated entities.

## Scope

- Convert static/rarely-changing chrome (HUD, timer bar, escort pods, bubbles/aura) from per-frame `Graphics` redraw to cached textures or a redraw-on-change scheme, preserving exact appearance.
- Where entities are repeatedly drawn as identical primitives, evaluate sprite-atlas or particle-emitter batching, and adopt it only if the profile shows a win and behaviour is unchanged.
- Apply in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/scenes/core/hudWiring.ts`) so gyms and `PlayScene` share the optimised path.
- Verify the Canvas fallback degrades cleanly (no `RenderTexture`-only assumption that breaks `Phaser.AUTO` on Canvas).
- Record before/after harness numbers and the profiler evidence on this item.

## Out of scope

- Changing visual design, colours, sizes or effects.
- Simulation-side allocation or collision work (sibling children).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The entity's/chrome's per-frame draw work is reduced and the change is measured: before/after harness numbers are recorded on this item, or the item is closed with evidence that this path is not material.
2. Visual output is unchanged: the affected elements render identically (pixel or model-level comparison test where practical; otherwise a documented visual check plus an assertion on draw geometry).
3. The optimised path lives in shared core code consumed by both gyms and `PlayScene`; no divergent copy exists.
4. Behaviour is unchanged — parity/equivalence suites pass and seeded runs are identical.
5. The Canvas fallback (`Phaser.AUTO` on a Canvas-only environment) still renders correctly, covered by a test or a documented manual verification.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateOptionsEscort` (~:1292), drop layer redraws (~:1557)
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — shield/force-field/thorns bubbles (~:1279), wave timer bar (~:4985)
- `src/scenes/core/hudWiring.ts` — `hud.refresh()` cadence
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — renderer config
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — record the measured win

## Dependencies

Blocked by the profiling child (evidence + baseline) and the harness child.

Publish the performance budget, the harness usage, the reference-machine definition, and the recorded baseline/results so future work has a single source of truth.

**User story:** As a maintainer, I want one document that states the frame-time budget, how to measure it, and where the current numbers live, so a regression is obvious and the target is not folklore.

- Create `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` covering:

## Goal

Prove, on the finished optimisation tree, that the parent's outcome targets are actually met — desktop ≥ 60 FPS and throttle-represented mobile ≥ 30 FPS at 100 late-game enemies — with gameplay behaviour unchanged — so the pass is complete on evidence rather than on optimism.

**User story:** As a player and as a developer, I want the 100-enemy scenario measured end-to-end on the finished build with the parity and determinism evidence attached, so the optimisation pass is provably complete and stays regression-guarded.

## Why

Parent acceptance criteria 4 (desktop target), 5 (mobile tier) and 7 (no behaviour change) are **outcome** criteria: they cannot be satisfied by any single optimisation child, only by the whole tree once children 1–6 have landed. Without a dedicated verification step, nothing in the plan actually runs the 60-second acceptance measurement or collects the parity evidence the parent promises.

## Scope

- Run `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` for a **60-second fixed-duration** run against `GymPerformance` (100 enemies, live fire) on **desktop browser** (Chromium) and the **packaged Electron app** on the recorded reference machine; capture p50/p95/max frame time, effective FPS and long-frame counts.
- Run the same harness with the **CPU-throttle profile (≥ 4× slowdown)** that represents the mobile tier, and require ≥ 30 FPS sustained.
- Assemble the **per-child before/after** harness numbers from children 4–6 (`_handleCollisions` broad-phase, hot-loop allocations, GPU offload/draw batching) next to the final numbers, so each win is attributable and the items that were closed as "not material" are visible as such.
- Collect **parity and determinism evidence**: the shared-core equivalence suite, the gym-parity docs guard, and a seeded `scripts/evaluate.mjs` bot run producing identical outcomes before/after the optimisation tree.
- If a target is missed: file new optimisation children ranked by measured hotspot share (parent AC6) and do **not** mark the parent complete on a missed target.

## Out of scope

- New optimisation work (children 4–6 own that; anything new becomes a child of this item or the parent).
- Changing the target, the throttle factor or the reference machine to make the bar pass.
- Gameplay, balance or wave changes.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Desktop target met:** a 60-second, 100-enemy run reports sustained ≥ 60 FPS with p95 frame time ≤ 16.7 ms and no sustained long-frame spike, on desktop browser **and** Electron, on the reference machine; the numbers are recorded on this item and in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
2. **Mobile tier measured and playable:** the same run under the fixed ≥ 4× CPU-throttle profile sustains ≥ 30 FPS with 100 enemies and the result is recorded; mobile is explicitly allowed the lower target.
3. **Per-child attribution:** per-child before/after harness numbers are recorded next to the final numbers, showing which change produced which measured win (and which structural suspects were closed as not material).
4. **Parity preserved:** the shared-core equivalence suite (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`), the gym-parity docs guard and the existing parity suites pass against the optimised tree.
5. **Determinism unchanged:** a seeded `scripts/evaluate.mjs` bot run produces identical outcomes before and after the optimisation tree; the comparison evidence is recorded.
6. **Missed targets are escalated, not hidden:** if either target is missed, new optimisation children are filed with measured impact, and the parent is left short of `in_review` with the shortfall recorded.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill).

# Intake Brief — Mini-Boss explosions should be huge

**Work item:** AH-0MVY06X16005EO8R (feature, medium)

**Headline:** Double the mini-boss's *own* explosions: the 10 anchored bursts
around its death point and the 20-burst finale go to at least 2× their current
geometry scale and per-burst particle count, while the swept-enemy and
scattered celebration bursts, the burst cadence, the 360 ms lifespan and the
reward-overlay wait all stay exactly as they are — so the mini-boss's death
reads as the biggest visual event in the level.

**Source request (verbatim):** "Increase the size of the mini-boss explosions.
They should be at least 2x the size in both scale and sprite count."

**Producer decisions (settled, all three asked during intake):**
**Q1 = (c) only the anchored + finale bursts** (the two roles clustered on the
mini-boss itself — the swept-enemy and scatter bursts keep today's sizing, and
the mini-boss body's inherited `Boss` death burst is untouched);
**Q2 = (a) per-burst particle count ×2** (burst *counts* stay at extras ≤30 /
10 anchored / 20 finale — the display length is unchanged);
**Q3 = (a) lifespan unchanged** at 360 ms per burst (no extra wait before the
reward overlay).

## Problem statement

The mini-boss defeat already produces a scripted 60-burst cascade, but every
burst in it was deliberately tuned **small**: the two roles that actually
belong to the mini-boss (its 10 anchored bursts at `ANCHORED_SCALE = 0.9`,
16 particles, and its 20-burst finale at `FINALE_SCALE = 1.2`, 20 particles)
are barely larger than a routine enemy pop, and the celebration filler around
them is smaller still (`ENEMY_SCALE = 0.8`/14, `SCATTER_SCALE = 0.7`/12). A
~2.95 s display of small, evenly sized circles does not read as "the biggest
kill in the level". The operator wants the mini-boss's own explosions to be
visibly huge.

## Users

- **Player** — the primary user; perceives the victory moment.
  - *As a player, when I finally destroy the mini-boss I want the explosions
    right on top of it to be visibly enormous, so the kill reads as a genuine
    spectacle rather than a cloud of small dots.*
- **Developer / designer** — tunes the display from named constants.
  - *As a developer, I can still reason about the sweep from its exported
    constants, and the "at least 2×" relationship for the mini-boss's own
    roles is pinned by a test so a future refactor cannot quietly shrink the
    display again.*
- **Tester (gym)** — verifies shipped behaviour.
  - *As a tester, the `GymMiniBoss` EXPLODE button shows exactly the same
    doubled bursts the game shows, because the sweep is one shared module.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Anchored and finale geometry at least 2×.** The two mini-boss roles'
  exported scale constants are doubled and their effective burst geometry
  (`size × scale` handed to `spawnExplosionParticles`) is therefore at least
  double today's: `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHORED_SCALE` 0.9 → **1.8** (base `size`
  16 ⇒ 14.4 px → 28.8 px) and `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_SCALE` 1.2 → **2.4**
  (base `size` 18 ⇒ 21.6 px → 43.2 px). Role ordering is preserved
  (`scatter < enemy < anchored < finale`).
- **AC2 — Anchored and finale particle count at least 2×.**
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHORED_PARTICLES` 16 → **32** and
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_PARTICLES` 20 → **40**.
- **AC3 — Out of scope, unchanged: swept-enemy and scatter bursts.** The
  enemy role (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ENEMY_SCALE = 0.8`,
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ENEMY_PARTICLES = 14`) and the scatter role
  (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_SCATTER_SCALE = 0.7`,
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_SCATTER_PARTICLES = 12`) keep their current values, and the
  scatter inset (`MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_INSET_PX = 24`) is unchanged because those
  bursts are not enlarged. The mini-boss **body's** own death burst (inherited
  from the shared `Boss`: `BOSS_RADIUS`, `resolvePatterns('boss')`) is also
  unchanged, so the final boss's death is unaffected.
- **AC4 — Cadence unchanged.** Burst counts (`max(0, 30 − n)` scatter, 10
  anchored, 20 finale), the per-role stagger windows, the finale cadence
  (2 bursts every 250 ms), the per-burst lifespan (360 ms) and therefore
  `plan.completionDelayMs` (~2.95 s) are **unchanged**. The reward overlay and
  the single wave/level advance still fire from `onComplete` after the last
  burst animates, at the same total delay as today.
- **AC5 — Shared code only, gym parity preserved.** The change is made once in
  `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts`; `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` both
  consume it unchanged, no divergent gym copy is introduced, and
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes.
- **AC6 — Determinism preserved.** No `Math.random()` is introduced; the plan
  for a given seed keeps the same burst count, order, delays and positions, so
  the existing seeded-replay tests still pass.
- **AC7 — Regression test pins the doubling and the non-scope.**
  `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.test.ts` gains assertions that, per
  role, the planned `scale` and `particleCount` are **at least 2×** the
  recorded baselines for anchored (0.9 / 16) and finale (1.2 / 20), and
  **exactly** the recorded baselines for enemy (0.8 / 14) and scatter
  (0.7 / 12) — plus an explicit assertion that burst counts and
  `completionDelayMs` are unchanged.
- **AC8 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §3.3.1 and
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (mini-boss defeat-sweep sections,
  ~:1608 and ~:1741) state the doubled anchored/finale magnitudes and note the
  deliberate size contrast with the unchanged swept-enemy/scatter bursts.
- **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (the
  dev-push gate is authoritative; no ad-hoc full-suite runs).

## Constraints

- **Particle budget.** Only the 30 mini-boss bursts (10 anchored + 20 finale)
  grow, from 16 → 32 and 20 → 40 particles, so peak concurrent particles rise
  by well under 2× (the enemy/scatter bursts are unchanged). Still one
  `Graphics` + one tween per burst — no new object count, no pooling work.
- **Cosmetic only.** The sweep keeps awarding no score, drops or telemetry;
  swept entities are still torn down through `destroySilently()`.
- **Audio untouched.** Blast cues and mix trims belong to AH-0MVVEI7FD004TR2M
  (SFX on mini-boss explosions); this item changes geometry/counts only.
- **No shared-default edits.** `Boss._playExplosion`, `BaseEnemy.playExplosion`
  and the `EXPLOSION_*` defaults in `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` must not
  change: the sweep passes explicit `scale`/`count`, so the doubling belongs in
  the sweep's own constants.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — the single mini-boss defeat sweep
  (pure planner + thin executor) introduced by AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z. Tunables in
  scope:
  - `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHORED_SCALE` (:160, 0.9),
    `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_SCALE` (:132, 1.2);
  - `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHORED_PARTICLES` (:141, 16),
    `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_FINALE_PARTICLES` (:129, 20);
  - planner base `size` literals: anchored 16 (:480), finale 18 (:509).
  Out of scope but adjacent: `..._ENEMY_SCALE` (:154, 0.8),
  `..._SCATTER_SCALE` (:157, 0.7), `..._ENEMY_PARTICLES` (:135, 14),
  `..._SCATTER_PARTICLES` (:138, 12), `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_INSET_PX` (:80, 24).
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — `spawnExplosionParticles` computes
  `effSize = size × scale`, uses an explicit `count` verbatim, and derives
  particle start radius (`0.5 × effSize`) and speed (`60 + 3 × effSize`) from
  it, so doubling the two roles' `scale` doubles both their visual radius and
  their particle travel distance. **No change needed in this file.**
- Consumers: `PlayScene` (`_damageMiniBoss` → `spawnMiniBossDeathSweep`;
  `_finaliseMiniBossDefeat` in `onComplete`) and `GymMiniBoss`
  (`explodeRandom`). Tests: `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.test.ts`
  (structural — roles, counts, delays, determinism, completion).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` lists `GymMiniBoss` as `parity` with the shared sweep,
  so no matrix change is expected from a tuning change inside that module.

## Desired change

Edit four constants in `miniBossDeathSweep.ts` (two scales, two particle
counts — anchored and finale), correct the now-stale role comments (anchored
"reduced particle count" and finale "denser than anchored" wording must
describe the new magnitudes honestly), add the AC7 regression test, and update
the two design documents (AC8). Nothing else changes: no new bursts, no timing
change, no inset change, no audio change, no gameplay change, no edit to
`explosionParticles.ts` or the `Boss`/`BaseEnemy` death paths.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — double
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHORED_SCALE`/`_FINALE_SCALE` and
  `MINI_BOSS_SWEEP_ANCHORED_PARTICLES`/`_FINALE_PARTICLES`; refresh the role
  comments.
- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.test.ts` — add the ≥2× (anchored,
  finale) and unchanged (enemy, scatter) assertions plus the unchanged
  burst-count / `completionDelayMs` assertions.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §3.3.1 records the doubled mini-boss
  burst magnitudes.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — the mini-boss defeat-sweep
  sections (~:1608 and ~:1741) record the doubled magnitudes.

## Related work

- **Mini Boss explosions (AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z, completed)** — created the
  shared defeat sweep this item enlarges; its ACs deliberately chose small
  per-burst geometry to fit 60 bursts in the particle budget. This item
  supersedes that sizing choice **for the mini-boss's own two roles only**.
- **SFX on mini-boss explosions (AH-0MVVEI7FD004TR2M, plan_complete)** —
  sibling concern (audio). Shares the burst plan and per-role mix trims; must
  not conflict. Sizing does not change roles, delays or completion, so either
  order is safe.
- **Explosions sould be explosions (AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, in_progress)** —
  reworks particle *rendering* (image-based shapes instead of circles) in
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`. Orthogonal in intent but touches the same
  VFX pipeline: if it lands first, these doubled counts/sizes must still hold;
  if this lands first, that item inherits the new magnitudes. This item should
  not need to touch `explosionParticles.ts` at all, so the two can proceed in
  parallel.
- **Strength of mini-boss and boss should raise with the fire power of the
  player (AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD, completed)** — same "the mini-boss should scale
  up" design philosophy, applied to HP rather than VFX.
- **Mini-boss defeat sweep documentation (AH-0MVROEO2I0014ILM)** and
  **Verification tests for mini-boss death sweep (AH-0MVROEJJR002HDLS)**
  (completed) — the docs sections and verification tests that AC8/AC7 touch.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Settled (producer): scope is the anchored + finale roles only;** particle
  count doubling applies per burst (not burst counts); lifespan stays 360 ms.
- **Risk — size contrast.** With the mini-boss bursts at 1.8/2.4 and everything
  else at 0.7/0.8, the display's focus moves decisively onto the death point.
  That is the intent (the mini-boss's own explosions should be huge); if the
  contrast proves too stark in the gym, the fix is a follow-up item (e.g.
  raising the scatter role), not silently shrinking the mini-boss bursts.
- **Risk — over-covering the death point.** 2.4× finale geometry inside the
  160 px `FINALE_SPREAD_PX` cluster may briefly wash out the mini-boss's own
  body during the finale. Accepted; if it hides the reward cue, revisit the
  spread in a follow-up rather than shrinking the bursts.
- **Risk — frame-time spikes.** 30 of the ~60 bursts now carry 32–40 particles
  instead of 16–20. Mitigated by staggered scheduling (2 finale bursts per
  250 ms) and one `Graphics` + one tween per burst.
- **Risk — edit collision** with AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY in
  `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` (see Related work). This item must not touch
  that file.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Extra ideas (enlarging the enemy/scatter roles,
  enlarging the mini-boss body burst, image-based bursts, screen shake,
  slow-motion) are **not** in scope; record them as linked work items instead.

## Appendix — clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 — Which explosions should double?**
  Options offered: (a) the four roles of the defeat sweep only; (b) the sweep
  **plus** the mini-boss body's own death burst; (c) only the anchored + finale
  bursts.
  **Agent's recommended option:** (a).
  — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply): (c) only the anchored + finale
  bursts.** Applied: AC1/AC2 cover anchored + finale; AC3 explicitly pins
  enemy, scatter and the body burst as unchanged.

- **Q2 — What does "2× sprite count" mean?**
  Options offered: (a) per-burst particle count ×2, burst count unchanged;
  (b) twice as many bursts (extras 30 → 60, anchored 10 → 20, finale 20 → 40,
  ~5.4 s display); (c) both.
  **Agent's recommended option:** (a).
  — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply): (a) per-burst particle count ×2.**
  Applied: AC2/AC4 — counts double per burst, burst counts and display length
  unchanged.

- **Q3 — Should the per-burst lifespan grow with the size?**
  Options offered: (a) keep 360 ms; (b) scale lifespan ~1.5–2×.
  **Agent's recommended option:** (a).
  — **Answer (Producer, interactive reply): (a) keep 360 ms.** Applied: AC4
  — lifespan and `completionDelayMs` (~2.95 s) unchanged.

- **Q4 — Is the increased particle load acceptable on the target hardware?**
  **Agent's recommended option:** yes — staggered bursts, one `Graphics` + one
  tween each; verify by eye in `GymMiniBoss` during implementation.
  Research: analysed `spawnExplosionParticles` — per-burst `Graphics`, no
  per-particle scene objects. — **OPEN QUESTION** (no answer needed to proceed;
  the visual check in `GymMiniBoss` covers it, and only 30 of ~60 bursts grow).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH87A3L004VOLD** – Strength of mini-boss and boss should raise with the fire power of the player (completed)
- **AH-0MTV8OV9V002D8B7** – 2 Bosses need renaming (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: boss, count, explosions, huge, increase (+6 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: boss, count, explosions, increase, least (+5 more)

# Teleport: 60 s recharge, no charge stack, pickup refreshes to ready

## Problem statement

Teleport currently regenerates far too quickly — **15 s at base, 5 s at the
upgrade cap** — and stockpiles up to **3 stored warps**, so a permanently owned
Teleport is almost always available and the defensive escape costs the player
nothing. Teleport should become a **single, slow-recharging escape**: one charge
every **60 s** at base (scaling to **20 s** at the upgrade cap), with a run-time
Teleport pickup refreshing the timer to ready immediately, and **no stored-charge
bookkeeping** at all.

## Users

- **As a player** who has just teleported out of danger, I want the escape to be
  gone for about a minute, so that evading a threat has a real cost and the
  ability is a decision rather than a permanent safety net.
- **As a player** flying through a Teleport drop while my Teleport is recharging,
  I want that pickup to make it ready again immediately, so chasing the drop is
  worth the risk.
- **As a player** who has permanently added Teleport to a loadout slot, I do not
  want to be offered a redundant "Teleport Charge" in the hold-full choice or
  see a Teleport wedge on the mini-boss wheel, because there is no charge left
  to grant.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the new model expressed as catalogue/level data
  and one shared seam, so the game and every gym cannot drift.

## Desired behaviour

1. **No charge stack.** Teleport has no stored-count, no FIFO pool and no cap-3
   counter. Its state is binary: **ready** (recharge timer 0) or **recharging**
   (timer > 0). The `teleportStacks` level axis is retired.
2. **Recharge interval.** Spending Teleport starts one recharge timer of the
   level-derived interval: **60 s at level 1 (base) → 20 s at the upgrade cap**
   (same 3:1 base:cap ratio and `k = 0.3` curve shape as today, applied to the
   new numbers). The axis stays charges-per-second (`base 1/60`, `cap 1/20`) so
   the monotonic non-decreasing rate contract holds.
3. **Pickup sets the timer to 0.** A run-time Teleport pickup makes Teleport
   **ready immediately** (recharge timer reset to 0), including while it is
   mid-recharge, on top of its existing temporary-level effect.
4. **Hold-full reward readies it.** A hold-full Teleport reward (which grants
   permanent ownership, i.e. a loadout slot) also leaves Teleport ready
   (timer 0).
5. **Usable only while held.** Teleport is available while it is held — either
   through an active temporary field-pickup level or through permanent
   ownership — and unavailable once a temporary window expires without
   permanent ownership (existing rule for unowned kinds).
6. **Rewards retire once permanently owned.** Once Teleport is permanently owned
   it is **excluded from the hold-full choice pool and the mini-boss wheel** —
   no `power-up-charge` offer, no wheel wedge, and no `+1 level` bonus grant for
   it. While it is *not* permanently owned it is still offered as a base
   `★ New` entry, which grants the slot.
7. **Auto-defence tie-break.** When both Phase Shift (charges > 0) and Teleport
   (ready) are available, the shared resolver picks **50/50** from the injected
   rng, regardless of Phase Shift's charge count. Only one available → that one;
   neither → nothing.
8. **HUD.** The Teleport row shows `ready` when the timer is 0 and
   `next in Ns` while recharging, with no stack suffix; the row greys out while
   recharging. Same HUD in the game and every gym.
9. **Gym↔game parity.** All of the above lives in shared code
   (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`,
   `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`); `PlayScene` and every gym inherit it. No
   gym override, no divergent copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single-use model.** Teleport exposes no stored-charge count anywhere
  (no `teleportStacks` axis, no FIFO pool, no `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP` special case
  for `teleport`); the store/registry report `ready` / `recharging` plus a
  remaining-seconds value. Verified by unit tests over `PowerUpLevelStore` and
  `EffectsRegistry`, and by the removal of the `teleportStacks` spec axis.
- **AC2 — Recharge interval 60 s → 20 s.** `teleportRechargeTime()` returns
  **60 s at level 1** and **20 s at the upgrade cap**, and is monotonically
  non-increasing across levels. Tested at the endpoints plus a monotonicity
  sweep.
- **AC3 — Spending starts the timer.** An automatic danger activation consumes
  the ready Teleport and starts one level-derived recharge timer; while the
  timer runs the ability is unavailable so no second warp can fire. Test:
  spend → unavailable → `tick(interval − ε)` still unavailable →
  `tick(+ε)` ready.
- **AC4 — Pickup (and hold-full reward) sets the timer to 0.** Collecting a
  Teleport drop while mid-recharge makes it ready immediately; a hold-full
  Teleport grant also leaves it ready. Tested for a field pickup during a
  cooldown and for the hold-full grant path.
- **AC5 — Rewards retire once permanently owned.** A permanently-owned Teleport
  produces no hold-full choice option (no `power-up-charge`) and no mini-boss
  wheel wedge, while an unowned Teleport is still offered as a `★ New` base
  entry. The exclusion is driven by catalogue data, never an
  `id === 'teleport'` branch. Tests cover both builders.
- **AC6 — Auto-defence tie-break is 50/50.** When both abilities are available
  the resolver returns `phase_shift` / `teleport` with equal probability from
  the injected rng, independent of Phase Shift's charge count; single-ability
  and neither-available cases unchanged. Seeded determinism tested.
- **AC7 — HUD reflects the new model.** The Teleport row renders `ready` /
  `next in Ns` (no stack count) and greys out while recharging, in `PlayScene`
  and in every gym that shows the shared HUD.
- **AC8 — Gym↔game parity holds.** The change is implemented once in shared
  code with no gym-specific override; the parity/equivalence suites
  (`src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) pass with the new model.
- **AC9 — Documentation updated.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 bullet,
  the teleport catalogue row, the §4.4.3 level table), `docs/BALANCING.md`, the
  catalogue description in `src/powerups/types.ts` and the code comments in
  `powerUpLevels.ts` / `effects.ts` / `choice.ts` all describe the single-use
  60 s → 20 s model; the `src/powerUpLevelingDocs.test.ts` assertions are
  updated to match.
- **AC10 — Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (run through the test skill / dev-push gate), and every new behaviour above
  is covered by a test that would fail if the behaviour regressed.

## Constraints

- **Data-only tuning** (producer answer Q3 = A): change the level-spec axis and
  the shared seams; do **not** add a runtime/rules-config knob for the recharge
  interval. Live gym tuning sliders stay with AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B.
- **Phase Shift is out of scope** — it keeps its charge pool and its 30 s → 10 s
  recharge. The shared charge-pool machinery must stay intact for Shield, Thorn
  Field, Phase Shift, Force Field and Mystery UFO.
- **No new offer kind** and no `id === 'teleport'` special case: express the
  model as catalogue data (a flag/axis that says "single-use, no charge pool,
  not rewardable when owned") so the shared builders stay kind-agnostic.
- **No new per-scene counters**: the recharge timer must live in the one
  `PowerUpLevelStore` (already ticked by the shared effect path).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed by the ship skill's release
  pipeline.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `teleportRechargeRate` axis
  (`base: 1/15`, `cap: 1/5`, `k: 0.3`) → `teleportRechargeTime()` 15 s → 5 s;
  `teleportStacks` axis (`base: 1`, `cap: 3`, `k: 0.5`); `_poolCap()` special-cases
  `phase_shift`/`teleport` to `POWER_UP_CHARGE_CAP`; per-charge timers in
  `_rechargeTimers` advanced by `tickRecharge()`; `consumeTeleport()`,
  `teleportStacks()`, `teleportRechargeTime()`, `consumableRechargeRemaining()`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `selectAutoDefence(phaseCharges, teleportStacks, rng)`
  compares available counts (greater count wins, exact tie → 50/50);
  `EffectsRegistry.consumeTeleport()`, `hasTeleport()`, `teleportStacks()`,
  `updateDanger()`/`_advanceAutoDefence` and the HUD snapshot builder
  (`stacks: teleportStacks`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (~1105) — `registry.consumeTeleport()` in the
  shared `triggerTeleport` path, consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `buildChargeOption()` produces
  `"+1 charge, regenerates every N s"` for an owned consumable;
  `buildOwnedPowerUpOffer()` dispatches on the catalogue `consumable` flag;
  `buildChoiceCandidates()` applies the six-slot gate.
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` — `isWheelKind()` / `orderedOwnedKinds()` /
  `buildWheelWedges()` build wedges from the shared `ownedIds`, and the bonus
  wedge grants `+1 level` on every owned kind.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Teleport row shows the stack count plus `next in Ns`
  (`buildHUDLabel`, `_powerUpRecharge`).

Discovered-from: AH-0MVUXH35J002WSAB (hold-full choice charge grant).

## Problem statement

A run checkpoint persists a consumable's **permanent level** but not its
**charge pool** or its in-flight recharge timers. `PlayScene._restoreCheckpoint`
replays `grantPermanentPowerUp` once per persisted level, and an owned
consumable is persisted at level 1 (a hold-full grant never levels it), so a
resumed run can only ever hold one charge and loses every spent-charge
regeneration clock. A run that banked three Shield charges and then resumed
silently loses two of them.

## Users (user stories)

- **As an arcade player** resuming from the last mini-boss checkpoint, I want
  the consumable charges I earned (and the recharge timers already running) to
  be exactly as I left them, so that Continue does not punish me for stopping.
- **As a player with a partially spent pool**, I want a charge that was
  mid-regeneration to keep regenerating on resume, so that the pool behaves as
  one continuous resource across the save.
- **As a maintainer**, I want the restored pool to flow through the one shared
  `PowerUpLevelStore` seam, so the checkpoint can never become a second
  charge counter that drifts from live play.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Save captures pools and timers.** A checkpoint written at a
  mini-boss defeat records, for each owned consumable (`shield`, `thorns`,
  `phase_shift`, `teleport`, `force_field`, `mystery_ufo`), its current charge
  count and the remaining seconds of every in-flight recharge timer.
- **AC2 — Resume restores them through the shared store seam.** A resumed run
  restores the pools and timers through `PowerUpLevelStore` (no second counter,
  no scene-local shadow state), and the resumed pool equals the saved pool
  exactly — including a pool of three charges and two partially elapsed
  recharge timers.
- **AC3 — Legacy payloads still resume.** A checkpoint payload with no charge
  fields loads and resumes exactly as today: the permanent-grant replay leaves
  each owned consumable with its single granted charge and no timers. The
  checkpoint schema version is **not** bumped (the new field is additive and
  optional), because the version gate rejects any payload stamped with another
  version.
- **AC4 — Tests pin both the round trip and the legacy fallback.** Unit tests
  cover the store snapshot/restore seam, the checkpoint round trip, defensive
  parsing, the slot-gate interaction and the legacy (no charge fields) resume
  path; the PlayScene tests cover save-side capture and resume-side restoration
  end to end.
- **AC5 — Defensive parsing and slot gate.** Malformed pool entries (unknown
  or non-consumable ids, negative/non-finite charges, non-finite timers, an
  absent array) are dropped or clamped rather than throwing, and a kind dropped
  by `capCheckpointLoadout`'s six-slot gate loses its charge pool too, so a
  resumed run can never hold charges for a kind it does not own.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.6 (the
  `ai_hell_checkpoint` storage row) and the `checkpointStore` module/version
  comment describe the persisted pool and the legacy fallback; the gym-parity
  note explains why no gym needs a change.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
  changes.

## Constraints

- **No schema-version bump.** `parseCheckpoint` rejects any payload whose
  `version` is not exactly `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` (3). AC3 requires legacy v3
  payloads to keep resuming, so the new field is optional and additive; a bump
  would be a breaking change and is explicitly out of scope.
- **One source of truth.** The pool and timers live in `PowerUpLevelStore`;
  the checkpoint only serialises and rehydrates them. The save path must read
  the same store instance the HUD and effect path read (`Player.getPowerUpLevelStore()`
  / `EffectsRegistry.levelStore()`), not `PowerUpLevelStore` internals.
- **Restore ordering.** Permanent grants are replayed first (that is what marks
  a consumable owned and sets its level-derived cap/interval), then the saved
  pool and timers are re-applied authoritatively, then lives — so the replay's
  single per-level grant can never leak into the saved pool.
- **Parity.** No gym implements checkpoint resume, so no gym scene needs a
  counterpart; the shared store API is consumed by the game and the gyms alike.
  Record this in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` reasoning if the matrix enumerates resume
  seams.
- **Scope guard.** Migrating consumables onto the charge pool for field
  pickups, HUD countdowns and effect-path convergence belong to the parent epic
  (AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW) and its follow-ups; this item only adds persistence.

## Existing state

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — `Checkpoint` v3 persists `weaponLevels` and
  `powerUpLevels` only; `toLevelList` is the defensive list parser;
  `capCheckpointLoadout` is the save-side six-slot gate.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_saveCheckpoint` builds the payload from
  `player.getPowerUpLevels()`; `_restoreCheckpoint` replays
  `grantPermanentWeapon` / `grantPermanentPowerUp` once per persisted level.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore` already owns
  `_charges` and `_rechargeTimers` with `consumableCharges`,
  `consumableChargeCap`, `consumableRechargeTime`,
  `consumableRechargeRemaining` (minimum timer only), `grantConsumableCharge`,
  `consumeConsumableCharge` and `tickRecharge`. It exposes **no** per-kind
  snapshot of all timers and **no** restore/set entry point.
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` — `grantPermanentPowerUp` is the single
  hold-full grant seam; for a consumable `collect(id, true)` adds exactly one
  charge and never raises the level.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.6 storage table row and §4.4.3 describe
  the checkpoint payload and the consumable charge model.

## Desired change

1. Add a small, pure `PowerUpLevelStore` snapshot/restore seam (e.g.
   `snapshotConsumablePools()` returning `{ id, charges, rechargeTimers }[]` and
   `restoreConsumablePools(entries)`) so a caller can read every in-flight timer
   and rehydrate it without touching private maps.
2. Extend `Checkpoint` with an optional `consumablePools` field (array of
   `{ id, charges, rechargeTimers }`), parsed defensively and dropped from
   payloads for any kind the six-slot gate removes; keep `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`
   at 3 and document the field as additive.
3. `PlayScene._saveCheckpoint` reads the pool snapshot from the player's single
   `PowerUpLevelStore`; `_restoreCheckpoint` re-applies it **after** the
   permanent-grant replay and before the lives restore.
4. Update the checkpoint documentation (§6.6 row, module/version comment) and
   add the tests named in AC5.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — new optional `consumablePools` field, defensive parser, slot-gate interaction, version-comment update
- `src/core/checkpointStore.test.ts` — round-trip, defensive-parse, legacy-fallback and slot-gate tests
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `snapshotConsumablePools` / `restoreConsumablePools` (or equivalent) on `PowerUpLevelStore`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — snapshot/restore seam tests, including partially elapsed timers
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_saveCheckpoint` capture and `_restoreCheckpoint` restore ordering
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — end-to-end save capture and resume restoration
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.6 `ai_hell_checkpoint` row and §4.4.3 charge-model note

## Related work

### Automated find-related report

Related work items:

- **AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2** – Shared consumable charge pool in PowerUpLevelStore (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3** – Registry one-event consumption and regeneration accessors (completed)
- **AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT** – Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore (completed)

Repository file matches:

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: checkpoint, charge, consumable, persisted
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, checkpoint, charge
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: checkpoint, charge

### Related work items (context)

- **AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2** — Shared consumable charge pool in `PowerUpLevelStore`
  (completed): the pool, timers, ownership flag and `tickRecharge` this item
  persists.
- **AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3** — Registry one-event consumption and regeneration
  accessors (completed): the effect-path accessors the resumed state feeds.
- **AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT** — Per-charge recharge engine in `PowerUpLevelStore`
  (completed): the per-charge timer semantics that must round-trip.
- **AH-0MVUXH35J002WSAB** — Hold-full choice charge grant (open, discovered-from
  source): owns the grant that makes a pool larger than one possible.
- **AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW** — Consumable charge pool epic (open): parent design
  decision that permanence is a regenerating charge pool, so pool contents are
  earned run state.
- **AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51** / **AH-0MVT1DYO5004UC4P** / **AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP**
  (completed) — the checkpoint save/resume, schema-v2 capacity and
  resumed-HUD seams this change extends.
- **AH-0MVT1DZRG000Q1US** (completed) — precedent for "apply capacity first,
  then clamp" restore ordering.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — restore ordering leak.** Replaying the permanent grant adds one
  charge; restoring the pool afterwards is what makes the pool authoritative.
  Mitigation: an explicit test asserting a saved pool of 0 charges survives a
  resume of an owned kind (the replay's charge must not reappear).
- **Risk — over-cap pool on resume.** A hand-edited payload could name more
  charges than the level-derived cap. Mitigation: clamp on restore to
  `consumableChargeCap` and drop non-consumable ids during parse; legitimate
  saves always fit, so AC2's "matches exactly" still holds.
- **Risk — second counter.** Mitigation: the snapshot/restore seam lives on
  `PowerUpLevelStore`; the checkpoint never reads or writes `_charges` /
  `_rechargeTimers` directly.
- **Assumption A1 —** timer values are persisted as **remaining seconds**
  (not absolute timestamps), so a resume continues each charge's countdown
  where it stopped; wall-clock time spent away from the game does not
  regenerate charges.
- **Assumption A2 —** ownership itself needs no new field: it is already
  re-derived from the replayed permanent-grant snapshot (`getLevels()` reports
  an owned consumable at level 1).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Field-pickup charge conversion, HUD countdowns and
  effect-path convergence are parent-epic work; extra opportunities are
  recorded as linked work items rather than absorbed here.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

No producer questions were required: the item's acceptance criteria resolve the
two design forks the repo search surfaced.

- **Q: Should the checkpoint schema version be bumped for the new pool fields?**
  — Answer (repository evidence, AC3): **no**. `parseCheckpoint` rejects every
  payload whose `version !== CHECKPOINT_VERSION`, and AC3 requires legacy
  payloads to keep resuming, so the field is additive and optional. Evidence:
  `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` version gate; `src/core/checkpointStore.test.ts`
  "a stale pre-wheel checkpoint version is rejected cleanly".
- **Q: Does any gym implement checkpoint resume, requiring a parity change?** —
  Answer (repository evidence): **no**. `PlayScene._restoreCheckpoint`'s doc
  comment records that no gym implements checkpoint resume, so only the shared
  `PowerUpLevelStore` seam is touched. Evidence:
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_restoreCheckpoint` documentation; AGENTS.md
  gym↔game parity rules.
- **Q: Where do the timer values come from, given the store exposes only a
  minimum?** — Answer (repository evidence): the store keeps all per-charge
  timers in `_rechargeTimers` but only surfaces `consumableRechargeRemaining`
  (the minimum), so the change adds a snapshot/restore accessor pair rather
  than a second store. Evidence: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`
  (`consumableRechargeRemaining`, `tickRecharge`, `_advanceRechargeTimers`).

# Timed upgrades show a timer

> **Headline:** Every HUD row with a live countdown gains a code-drawn arc ring
> around its icon that fills as a charge recharges (and drains as a timed window
> expires), so the player can read timing at a glance instead of parsing the
> `next in Ns` text.

## Problem statement

Timer-driven upgrades are readable only as **text**: a recharging consumable row
appends `next in Ns` to its label, a timed window shows `Ns` in the value column,
and an owned-but-empty pool is greyed out. Mid-combat the player must read and
parse that text to know how close the next charge (or the end of the window) is.
The upgrade's own icon — the thing the player already uses to identify the item —
carries no timing information at all.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (primary).**
  - *As a player*, while my Teleport pool is empty, I want to see **at a glance**
    how far the recharge has progressed, so I can decide whether to hold position
    or push into danger.
  - *As a player*, while a timed upgrade is running (e.g. Speed Boost), I want the
    icon to show how much of the window is left, so I do not have to read the
    seconds column while dodging.
  - *As a player*, when a charge becomes available — or a window ends — I want the
    indicator to read unambiguously without reading a number.
- **Producer/operator.** One consistent timing affordance on every countdown row,
  so the HUD never mixes "some rows have gauges, some do not".

## Existing state (verified in the repo)

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` renders one row per power-up as `[icon Graphics, label Text,
  value Text]` (weapon rows likewise via `_addWeaponRow`) and rebuilds every row
  on each `refresh()`, called per frame from `HUD.update()`. Teardown goes through
  `_rowObjects`.
- Icons are code-drawn: `drawPowerUpIcon(...)` / `drawWeaponIcon(...)` in
  `src/powerups/icons.ts`, drawn at **8 px** at `ICON_X = 10` inside a
  **`HUD_ROW_HEIGHT = 22`** row; the label column starts at `NAME_X = 24`.
- Four countdown sources exist today, and they are **not** uniform in the data
  they expose:
  1. **Consumable recharge** (`Teleport`, `Phase Shift`, `Shield`, `Thorn Field`,
     `Force Field`, `Mystery UFO`): `EffectsRegistry.consumableRechargeRemaining(id)`
     → the soonest in-flight timer. `PowerUpLevelStore._rechargeTimers` keeps
     `number[]` of **remaining seconds only** — the per-timer duration captured at
     consumption is not stored, so a fraction is not currently derivable.
  2. **Power-up timed window** (e.g. `Speed Boost`, `Salvage`):
     `powerUpTemporaryRemaining(id)`; the internal `_timed` entries already hold
     `{ duration, remaining }`.
  3. **Weapon field-pickup window**: `activeWeapons()` already returns
     `WeaponEffect { duration, remaining, tempWindow }`.
  4. **Permanent Orbital Strike cadence**: `strikeNextBoltSeconds()` plus
     `strikeInterval()`.
- The empty-pool state already exists: `HUD._isPowerUpGreyed(id)` paints icon,
  label and value with the shared `POWER_UP_GREY_COLOUR`; non-slot rows are dimmed
  via `NON_SLOT_ROW_ALPHA`.
- A proportional-fill precedent exists on the same HUD (the mineral hold bar,
  `_drawMineralBar`, with a `MINERAL_BAR_MIN_FILL` legibility floor).
- The HUD is one shared class used by `PlayScene` and every gym that shows it, so
  an indicator implemented here is game↔gym-parity correct by construction.
- No mask/clip usage exists anywhere in `src/` (`createGeometryMask` is unused),
  which is why the operator chose the mask-free arc form.

## Desired change

Every HUD row that has a **live countdown** gains a **sweeping arc ring around its
icon** — code-drawn, no mask, no external asset — that shows the fraction of that
countdown currently available:

- **Arriving** countdowns (a charge recharging, the next Orbital Strike bolt):
  the ring **fills clockwise from empty to complete** as the wait elapses; empty
  the moment the charge is spent / the bolt fires, complete when the event is due.
- **Expiring** countdowns (a timed power-up window, a weapon field-pickup window):
  the ring **drains clockwise from complete to empty** as the window burns down;
  complete at pickup, empty at expiry.
- Rows with **no live countdown** (pool full / permanent `∞` / no pending bolt) draw
  **no ring** and render exactly as today.

Ring geometry (proposed, to be tuned during implementation): centred on the row
icon, radius just outside the 8 px glyph, thin stroke (≈2 px) in the item's own
palette colour (`ICON_COLORS[id]` / weapon icon colour), swept from 12 o'clock
clockwise, with a minimum visible sweep while the timer is live so a nearly-done
countdown never flickers to invisible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single progress seam.** The arc fraction comes from one shared, pure
  helper (e.g. `resolveCountdownFraction({ remaining, total, mode })`) plus
  registry/store accessors; no per-kind fraction arithmetic is duplicated in the
  HUD, and the game and every gym read the same seam.
- **AC2 — Arriving countdowns fill.** For a consumable recharge and for the
  permanent Orbital Strike cadence, the rendered fraction rises monotonically from
  `0` at the spend/fire instant to `1` when the charge returns / the next bolt is
  due, and it agrees with the same timer the existing `next in Ns` label reports
  at every refresh (icon and text can never disagree).
- **AC3 — Expiring countdowns drain.** For a power-up timed window and a weapon
  field-pickup window, the fraction starts at `1` and decreases monotonically to
  `0` at expiry, derived from the window's own captured `duration`, never from a
  hard-coded TTL.
- **AC4 — No countdown, no ring.** Rows with nothing counting down (full pool,
  permanent-only `∞` row, no pending bolt, non-timer rows such as Magnet level or
  the lives row) draw no arc and are otherwise byte-identical to today's output
  (regression test).
- **AC5 — Reset on reuse.** Spending a returned charge restarts the ring from empty
  (no stale complete ring), and a refreshed/restarted window restarts from complete
  (no stale empty ring).
- **AC6 — Multiple in-flight charges.** With several charges recharging, the ring
  reflects the **soonest-returning** charge — the same timer the label reports —
  and the ` ×N` charge count is unchanged.
- **AC7 — Legibility and layout invariants.** The ring fits inside the row without
  moving the label, value, marker or budget columns; it reads at 8 px icon size;
  the state is distinguishable without relying on hue alone (arc length + the
  existing shared grey); the greyed/non-slot alpha rules are preserved.
- **AC8 — No leak.** Rebuilding the HUD each frame does not grow the scene child
  list: after many `refresh()` calls the rendered-object count is bounded
  (regression test alongside the existing teardown assertions).
- **AC9 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests for the pure fraction helper (all four
  sources, edge cases at `0`, `1`, zero/undefined totals), HUD row-model tests
  asserting the fraction each row reports, a rendering test that the arc Graphics
  carries the expected fraction, and per-state coverage for at least one kind of
  each of the four countdown sources — written to fail before the implementation.
- **AC10 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 HUD presentation
  paragraph) and the `src/ui/HUD.ts` module docblock describe the ring, its two
  directions and the "no live countdown, no ring" rule; the progress seam is
  explained in code comments.
- **AC11 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Code-first visuals:** no new art assets, no new runtime dependencies (repo
  convention for every icon and effect).
- **Mask-free:** the chosen form must not use a geometry/bitmap mask; `Graphics`
  arc drawing only (no mask precedent exists in `src/`).
- **Per-frame rebuild:** `HUD.refresh()` destroys and recreates row objects every
  frame; the arc must ride on the row's existing `Graphics` object (or be torn down
  with it) and must not add measurable per-frame churn.
- **Single clock:** recharges keep advancing only through the shared
  `EffectsRegistry.tick` → `PowerUpLevelStore.tickRecharge` path; no second timer.
- **No behaviour change:** recharge timings, caps, grey-out rules, value-column
  semantics and the `next in Ns` text stay exactly as they are.
- **Backwards-compatible store change:** adding a per-timer total to
  `_rechargeTimers` must keep `tickRecharge` / `_advanceRechargeTimers` semantics
  and their existing tests green.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — row model gains the fraction; `_addRow` / `_addWeaponRow` draw
  the ring around the row icon.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — shared ring-drawing helper (same palette, same
  8 px glyph geometry).
- `src/ui/hudCountdown.ts` *(new, or a small helper inside `icons.ts`)* — the pure
  `resolveCountdownFraction` seam.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — store per-timer total and expose
  `consumableRechargeProgress(id)`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — registry projections: consumable recharge progress,
  power-up window total (weapons already expose `duration`/`remaining`).
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 HUD presentation paragraph.

## Related work

- AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW — Consumable upgrades should not be endless (parent of the
  charge-pool model).
- AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6 — HUD charge count and regeneration countdown (shipped the
  `next in Ns` text this item complements).
- AH-0MV82I97Y007MB6M — HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows (shipped the
  greyed empty state the ring refines).
- AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP — *HUD recharge countdown indicator (recharge follow-up)*
  (open). Its text half already shipped via AH-0MVUXH2DH0032UJ6 and this item is
  the visual half; recommendation is to close it as superseded rather than keep
  two indicators (not closed by this intake).
- AH-0MV82IAM7004KOYQ — Recharge-complete audio cue (open, **out of scope**).
- AH-0MVY3IGRC00954UD — Checkpoint does not persist consumable charge pools
  (open, **out of scope**).
- AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR — Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge.
- AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT — Per-charge recharge engine in PowerUpLevelStore.
- AH-0MV82I8IL0012RXY — Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence (the
  shared clock the ring reads, never a second timer).
- AH-0MVUXH0T0001N3C2 — Shared consumable charge pool in PowerUpLevelStore.
- AH-0MVUXH1LV0058TS3 — Registry one-event consumption and regeneration
  accessors (the seam the new progress projection extends).
- AH-0MVUXH3X60078QR3 — Consumable charge scene wiring and gym parity (the
  shared wiring that makes the ring game↔gym correct for free).
- AH-0MVRE6N08001TE4V — Orbital Strike cadence (the `next in Ns` timer the ring
  also reflects).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 / §4.4.3 — the documented HUD presentation
  and the recharge-interval table the projection reads.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Ring vs. glyph at 8 px:** a ring just outside an 8 px glyph is roughly 9–10 px
  across inside a 22 px row. Risk: it reads as a dot rather than a gauge.
  Mitigation: tune radius/stroke during implementation and validate in the
  power-up leveling gym; if it is unreadable, escalate to the operator rather than
  silently switching form.
- **Per-frame arc churn:** one extra arc path per countdown row per frame. Mitigated
  by drawing on the row's existing `Graphics` (no new objects) and AC8.
- **Multi-charge ambiguity:** several timers can run at once; the ring shows only
  the soonest (AC6), so it must not be read as "one timer per charge". The ` ×N`
  count and the seconds label remain the disambiguators.
- **Store change blast radius:** `_rechargeTimers` becomes a richer structure;
  `tickRecharge`, `_advanceRechargeTimers`, `reset` and their tests must keep their
  current semantics.
- **Visual noise:** six rings can be on screen at once. If playtesting reads as
  clutter, the fallback is to ring only the rows whose pool is not full — a
  documented divergence to be raised with the operator, not decided silently.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the recharge-complete audio cue, checkpoint persistence of
  pools, per-charge segmented gauges, timer-balance changes and any in-world (non
  HUD) indicator are **not** part of this item; record them as linked work items
  instead of widening scope.
- **Assumption:** the value column keeps `∞`/`Ns` exactly as today; the ring is
  additive information, never a replacement.
- **Assumption:** the shared HUD is the only surface that needs the change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope: which timers drive the indicator?** *(options: (a) consumable
  recharge pools only, (b) also timed effect windows, (c) every countdown row
  including the permanent Orbital Strike next-bolt cadence)* — Answer (operator,
  interactive reply, 2026-11-03): **"(c)"** — every countdown row. Recorded in

  window, weapon field-pickup window, permanent Orbital Strike cadence.

  (b) sweeping arc/ring around the icon, (c) thin bar under the icon)* — Answer

  around the icon. Recorded as the mask-free constraint and the ring geometry
  above. Research: `src/` contains no `createGeometryMask`, `setMask` or
  `createBitmapMask` usage, so (a) would have introduced a new rendering pattern;
  (b) needs only `Graphics` arcs.
- **Q3 — Keep the `next in Ns` text?** *(options: (a) keep, (b) remove, (c) keep but
  shorten)* — **OPEN QUESTION** (asked 2026-11-03, not answered in the round).
  Proceeding on the agent's recommended default **(a) keep**, which preserves the
  documented GDD behaviour and the several tests pinned to the label; the operator
  may switch to (b)/(c) before implementation and only the AC list changes (the

- **Q — agent research, no operator input needed:** *Is a progress fraction
  available today?* — Answer (agent, repo inspection): **no** for consumable
  recharges (`PowerUpLevelStore._rechargeTimers` stores remaining seconds only);
  **yes** for power-up timed windows (`_timed` keeps `duration`), weapon windows

  `strikeNextBoltSeconds()`). Evidence: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`,
