# SFX mix — trim explosions and enemy weapons by ~40% — Intake Brief

> Trim the **effective playback gain by 40%** (linear ×0.6) for two cue families —
> enemy weapon fire and explosion/destruction booms — so combat reads less
> cluttered and the player's own weapon, pickup and UI feedback sits forward in
> the mix. The trim is a **runtime** mix change through the existing named-constant
> seam in `src/audio/effects.ts`; baked WAVs, recipes and checksums are untouched.

## Problem Statement

Explosions and enemy weapon fire dominate the game's audio mix. Enemy shots and
destruction booms currently play at or near full runtime gain (the Tank/Scout
and Phaser fire sequences were already halved by earlier items, everything else
is unscaled), so dense waves turn into a wall of enemy noise that masks the
player's own fire, impacts and pickup feedback. The producer asked for
"the audio for explosions and enemy weapons" to come down by **around 40%**.

## Users

- **The player** in wave combat, hearing their own weapons, pickups and the
  enemy mix together.
- The player during end-of-wave, boss and mini-boss destruction beats, where
  layered explosion cues currently stack at full gain.

## User Stories

- As a player, enemy fire (Tank, Scout, Phaser, Diver, Boss, Swarm) sits about
  40% quieter than today, so I can still read incoming fire by direction and
  timing without it drowning my own weapons.
- As a player, enemy/player/boss/diver destruction booms and the short
  bullet-destruction, swarm-volley, force-field-break and boss-hit cues are
  about 40% quieter, so a mass kill reads as impact rather than noise.
- As the audio maintainer, I can retune the whole family from one named
  constant per family instead of hunting per-cue literals.

## Scope (producer-confirmed)

Producer answers: **Q1 = A** (all enemy fire sequences incl. advance/warmup
tells), **Q2 = A + follow-up A** (destruction booms **plus** the
explosion-adjacent tick/volley/hit cues, **not** the player-weapon impact
family), **Q3 = A** (relative trim: ×0.6 on today's effective gain).

### Enemy weapons — current → target effective gain

| Cue | Current gain | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `playTankAdvanceCue`, `playTankFireSound` | 0.5 (`TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) | **0.30** |
| `playScoutAdvanceCue`, `playScoutFireSound` | 0.5 (`TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) | **0.30** |
| `playPhaserAdvanceCue`, `playPhaserFireSound` | 0.5 (`PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`) | **0.30** |
| `playDiverFireSound` | 1.0 (unscaled) | **0.60** |
| `playBossFireSound` | 1.0 (unscaled) | **0.60** |
| `playSwarmBurstSound` | 1.0 (unscaled) | **0.60** |

### Explosions and explosion-adjacent cues — current → target

| Cue | Current gain | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `playDestructionSound` | 1.0 × caller `volume` | **0.6 × caller `volume`** |
| `playDiverDestructionSound` | 1.0 | **0.60** |
| `playBossDestructionSound` | 1.0 × caller `volume` | **0.6 × caller `volume`** |
| `playPlayerDestructionSound(volumeScale)` | `volumeScale` (currently 1.0 from `playerDeathJuice`) | **0.6 × `volumeScale`** |
| `playVictoryExplosionSound` | caller `volume` (0.55 default) | **0.6 × caller `volume`** |
| `playBulletDestructionSound` | 1.0 | **0.60** |
| `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound` (alias of the bullet-destruction asset) | 1.0 | **0.60** |
| `playBossHitSound` | 1.0 | **0.60** |

`playSwarmBurstSound` appears in both families — it must be scaled **exactly
once** (0.60), never twice (0.36).

### Explicitly out of scope

Enemy spawn, Diver dive-loop/dive-start, Boss spawn/phase-cue/phase-transition,
thruster hum, the whole player-weapon **fire and impact** family
(`playCannon*`, `playRicochet*`, `playCluster*`, `playOptions*`, `playNova*`,
`playSpread*`, `playDual*`, `playRapid*`, `playRailgun*`, `playShardSwarm*`,
`playRearGuard*`, `playBroadside*`, `playHeavySlug*`, `playMortar*`, `playArc*`,
`playWaveLaser*`), Force Field reflect, power-up/pickup cues, countdown tick,
mineral tinkle, Mystery UFO cues, victory/defeat stingers and the non-explosive
victory firework accents (`playVictoryCrackSound`, `playVictoryPopSound`,
`playVictorySparkleSound`). These keep their current gains; any further trim is
a separate item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Enemy weapon cues land on the target gains.** Effective gain asserted
  through the recording provider (`recording.plays[].volume`): Tank/Scout and
  Phaser advance+fire = `0.30`; Diver fire, Boss fire, Swarm burst = `0.60`.
  The advance→fire no-gap scheduling (`TANK_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`,
  `SCOUT_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`, `PHASER_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION`) is unchanged.
- **AC2 — Explosion cues land on the target gains without losing caller trims.**
  `playDestructionSound`, `playDiverDestructionSound`, `playBossDestructionSound`,
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`, `playVictoryExplosionSound`,
  `playBulletDestructionSound`, `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound` and
  `playBossHitSound` all play at 40% below today's effective gain. Caller-supplied
  volumes **compose multiplicatively** rather than being replaced: the mini-boss
  death sweep (0.55/0.30/0.40/0.65 → 0.33/0.18/0.24/0.39), victory fireworks
  (0.55 → 0.33) and `playPlayerDestructionSound`'s `volumeScale` argument all
  carry through. `playSwarmBurstSound` and the `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound`
  alias (which dispatches the bullet-destruction asset directly, bypassing the
  bullet-destruction wrapper) are each scaled **exactly once**.
- **AC3 — No collateral mix changes.** Every cue listed as out of scope keeps
  its current effective gain, and master volume/mute (`setSfxVolume`/
  `setSfxMuted`) behaviour is unchanged. The trim lives in the shared
  `src/audio/effects.ts` seam, so the game and every gym get identical gains.
- **AC4 — One named tunable per family, runtime only.** The trims are expressed
  as exported named constants (with comments recording the −40% rationale and the
  ×0.5 precedent they compose with), not inline literals. No baked asset,
  ToneForge recipe, manifest entry or `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` changes —
  `npm run build-audio:verify` and `node scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs` stay
  green (baked assets remain inside the AC2 amplitude tiers / AC3 A-minor scale
  guard).
- **AC5 — Testing and validation.** Changed-scope tests (`src/audio/**`, plus
  `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep` and `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice` where caller
  volumes compose) are run through the test skill and pass; the assertions prove
  the target gains, the single-application rule and the preserved caller trims.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` gains a section
  recording the −40% trim and the resulting per-cue effective gains;
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` notes the newly runtime-trimmed cues;
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`'s volume-scaling precedent list gains
  the explosion family. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Runtime trim only.** Baked assets are pinned by the amplitude-tier and
  A-minor guards; re-rendering to hit −40% would break those guards and is not
  the established mechanism (precedent: `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`,
  `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE`).
- **Compose, don't clobber.** Several explosion callers already pass
  per-context trims (mini-boss sweep, victory fireworks, player death). The new
  family scale must multiply those, not overwrite them.
- **Single seam.** Gains are applied in `src/audio/effects.ts` (the one funnel
  used by PlayScene and every gym); no per-scene volume logic.
- **No new cue, no removed cue, no settings/UI change** — this is a mix trim.

## Existing State

- Playback: `playCue()` → `provider.play(url, { volume })` → per-source gain ×
  the shared master gain (`src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`).
- Existing enemy trims: `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5` (Tank/Scout
  advance+fire, `AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3`), `PHASER_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5`
  (Phaser advance+fire, `AH-0MVFHE6VP006GEX0`). Diver fire, Boss fire and Swarm
  burst are unscaled.
- Explosion wrappers are unscaled; the destruction cues are beat-quantised via
  `playExplosionCue` (16th-note accent grid, `AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3`).
- `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound()` calls `playCue('playBulletDestructionSound')`
  directly, so a wrapper-only trim would silently miss it.
- Post-rebalance baked peaks for the scoped set are ≤ 0.42, so a ×0.6 runtime
  trim leaves ample headroom (loudest effective peak ≈ 0.25).

## Desired Change

Apply a uniform ×0.6 mix scale to the two families through named constants,
composed with the existing per-cue scales and caller volumes, and assert the
resulting effective gains in the audio tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new family mix constants; scale applied to the scoped
  wrappers (and to the force-field-break alias path) so caller `volume` composes.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — per-cue effective-gain assertions, single-application
  checks, no-collateral-change checks.
- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — verify caller trims still compose
  (no constant change expected).
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` — verify victory firework volume still composes.
- `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — verify `volumeScale` composition.
- `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` — new trim section + effective-gain table.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — runtime-trim notation for the new cues.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — volume-scaling precedent list.

## Risks, Assumptions and Mitigations

- **Risk — missed dispatch path.** Cues dispatched outside their public wrapper
  (the force-field-break alias) would keep full gain. *Mitigation:* scale at a
  point both paths cross and assert the alias explicitly (AC2).
- **Risk — double scaling.** `playSwarmBurstSound` belongs to both families.
  *Mitigation:* single-application assertion (AC2).
- **Risk — over-quiet enemy tells.** 0.3 × the tank-advance asset (peak 0.108)
  is ≈ 0.03 peak; still audible but close to the ambience floor.
  *Mitigation:* the trim is relative and uniform, so fire cues keep their
  balance against each other and against the beat grid; a follow-up item can
  retune per-cue if the producer hears a tell disappear.
- **Assumption —** "reduce around 40%" means a linear gain multiplier of 0.6,
  not −40 dB (which would be near-silence).
- **Assumption —** runtime constants are the correct mechanism (precedent), so
  baked assets and the balance guards stay untouched.
- **Scope-creep risk —** player-weapon impacts, boss phase cues and the
  non-explosive victory firework accents were considered and excluded; if the
  producer wants them trimmed, they become linked follow-up items rather than
  scope here.

## Related Work

- **Reduce the volume of shots for Tank and Scout (AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3)** —
  established `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE = 0.5` and the "advance tells are
  part of the fire sequence" decision this item composes with.
- **Phaser fire-sequence volume trim + verification (AH-0MVFHE6VP006GEX0)** —
  precedent for a named per-family runtime trim with docs updates.
- **Balance the levels of all enemy sounds (AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q)** — parent epic
  that pinned baked amplitude tiers and the A-minor scale guard; its tier
  targets stay valid because this trim is runtime-only.
- **Analysis report: enemy cue tf analyze metrics (AH-0MVCRR10A001OM2K)** and
  **`docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md`** — current baked peaks/RMS for every cue in
  scope.
- **Explosions timed with the beat (AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3)** — the
  `playExplosionCue` accent grid and voice caps the destruction cues run
  through; unchanged here.
- **Limit the number of each explosion and weapon sound that can fire (AH-0MVH8RQR7007QG8E)**
  — the other mix-clipping lever (per-cue concurrent-voice cap); unchanged here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which cues count as "enemy weapons"?** Options: (A) all enemy fire
  sequences — Tank/Scout/Phaser advance+fire, Diver fire, Boss fire, Swarm
  burst; (B) shot cues only, advance tells excluded; (C) Tank/Scout/Phaser only.
  **Recommended:** A — advance tells are part of the same audible fire sequence,
  as confirmed for the earlier Tank/Scout trim. **Answer (producer): "A"**.
  Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 — Which cues count as "explosions"?** Options: (A) the destruction
  booms — enemy, diver, boss, player, victory explosion; (B) enemy destruction
  only; (C) A plus bullet-destruction ticks and swarm/impact one-shots.
  **Recommended:** A — the five genuinely explosion-class cues; cutting small
  ticks would cost gameplay feedback. **Answer (producer): "C"**.
  Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2 follow-up — which tick/volley/hit cues join the trim?** Options: (A)
  explosion-adjacent only — `playBulletDestructionSound`,
  `playSwarmBurstSound`, `playEnemyForceFieldBreakSound`, `playBossHitSound`;
  (B) A plus the full ~16-cue player-weapon impact family; (C) bullet
  destruction + swarm burst only. **Recommended:** A — keeps the change inside
  "explosions and enemy-weapon noise"; B would also quiet the player's own
  weapon-hit feedback, which is a separate mix decision.
  **Answer (producer): "A"**. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q3 — "Reduce around 40%" — from what baseline?** Options: (A) another ×0.6
  on today's effective gain (already-trimmed Tank/Scout/Phaser 0.5 → 0.30,
  unscaled cues 1.0 → 0.60); (B) absolute effective gain 0.4 for every scoped
  cue; (C) only reduce cues still at 1.0 and leave the 0.5 trims.
  **Recommended:** A — a uniform relative trim preserves the relative balance
  already established between enemy fire cues.
  **Answer (producer): "A"**. Source: interactive reply.

- **Research note (no question needed) —** repo inspection of
  `src/audio/effects.ts`, `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts`,
  `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` and `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` established
  the current gains, the caller-supplied volume sites (mini-boss sweep, victory
  fireworks, player death) and the force-field-break alias path; the brief's
  scope tables are derived from that inspection, not from producer estimates.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVFHE6VP006GEX0** – Phaser fire-sequence volume trim + verification (post-audit) (completed)
- **AH-0MVSAJMLL00835T8** – ToneForge UFO cue bake (completed)
- **AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3** – Reduce the volume of shots for Tank and Scout (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: 16th, absolute, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+380 more)

## Problem

`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — `the 12-hex ring 2 grind lands inside the 90–120-minute budget` runs a CPU-bound simulation (`simulateRingTiming`, seeds 1/2/3, 12 deployments each) and declares a hard `60_000 ms` vitest timeout. On a quiet host the whole test takes ≈21 s; when the machine is oversubscribed it takes >100 s and fails with `Test timed out in 60000ms`.

Observed 2026-11-03 11:33 UTC on a 16-core host at load average ≈49 (four other suites running, AI_Hell and other repos):

```
FAIL  |unit| src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts > ring timing: real arena evidence > the 12-hex ring 2 grind lands inside the 90–120-minute budget
Error: Test timed out in 60000ms.
 ❯ src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts:319
```

The same tree had a green full-suite run 50 minutes earlier (419 files / 9517 tests, exit 0), and the test passes in isolation.

## Why it matters

Any session finishing work while the host is loaded gets a red full-suite gate caused purely by CPU contention, which then has to be classified as infrastructure and re-run — wasted effort, and easily mistaken for a genuine regression in an unrelated change.

## Suggested fix

Give the heavy ring-timing simulations realistic timeout headroom (e.g. `120_000`–`180_000 ms`) or move the ring-2 grind measurement behind a slow/heavy test lane that the default unit run does not include. Prefer explicit per-test timeouts over a global bump so fast tests stay fast to fail.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A contended-host run of the unit suite no longer fails the ring-timing tests on timeout (demonstrated by the chosen timeout/lane change and a comment recording the measured idle vs contended durations).
2. The ring-timing assertions themselves (budget window, determinism, deployment counts) are unchanged in meaning.
3. Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Problem

A full-suite run started from the **main checkout** can be corrupted mid-run when a concurrent session's `implement.py finish` fast-forwards the shared checkout's local `dev` (commit → ff → push) while the suite is still executing. Vitest transforms/imports test files lazily over the whole run, so files rewritten by the incoming commit are picked up part-way through: the run then executes the *new* test files against the *old* sources and reports failures that exist in neither tree.

Observed on 2026-11-03 (discovered-from:AH-0MW0M82U40059AKD): a full-suite post-push verification started in the main checkout at `86f39d30` reported 13 failures (`src/core/featureFlags.test.ts` ×12, `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` ×1). `06ecf940` (AH-0MVZ4S9ZU004GXUM, the Hangar War feature-flag flip) landed in the main checkout at ~12:57, mid-run, rewriting exactly those two test files. Re-running the full suite in a stable worktree at `86f39d30` was green (`421 files / 9578 tests`), and both files pass in isolation at `06ecf940` (`32 tests`). The run reported **no** `live_repo_mutation` notice, so the corruption was invisible to the caller — it looks like a genuine test failure.

Why it matters: gate evidence (`run_tests.py --scope full`) and post-push verification are audit inputs. A mixed-tree result can create spurious critical `test-failure` items and can make a *green* tree look red (or, worse, a red tree look green).

## Suggested approach (for discussion)

- Detect the mutation in `run_tests.py`: record the checkout's `HEAD` + a cheap tree fingerprint before the suite starts and re-check it after, emitting the existing `live_repo_mutation` notice (and a non-zero/again-invalid cache entry) when they differ. This covers any command that runs long enough to overlap another session's finish.
- Alternatively (or additionally) have `implement.py finish` refuse/queue while another session's test run holds the repo test-slot lock, so a finish cannot fast-forward the checkout under an in-flight suite.
- Consider running main-checkout post-push verification from a pinned worktree/detached tree rather than the shared checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A full-suite run whose checkout moved mid-run is reported as such (machine-readable notice naming the before/after commit), never silently as a test failure, and its cache entry cannot be consumed as gate evidence.
2. A regression test covers the detection (simulated mid-run `HEAD` change → notice raised).
3. Documented in the test-skill reference (notice codes / gate diagnostics).

## Links

- Discovered while closing AH-0MW0M82U40059AKD (triage false positive from leaked test stderr).
- Evidence: full run at `86f39d30` in a stable worktree green (421 files / 9578 tests); the same suite in the main checkout failed 13 tests after `06ecf940` was fast-forwarded in mid-run.

# Halve per-kill power-up drops and remove Extra Life from reward screens

## Problem statement

Too many power-ups — and in particular **Extra Life** — reach the player during a
run, so the 3-life start and the 5-life cap stop feeling meaningful and the
hold-full/mini-boss reward overlays are dominated by a pickup that trivialises
survivability. The operator wants the **per-kill power-up drop rate halved**, the
**asteroid Extra Life source stopped**, and **Extra Life removed from the
hold-full choice and mini-boss reward screens**, keeping it only as a rare field
pickup.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a run where lives are scarce and earned: fewer drops overall,
  no "free" lives from rocks, and reward overlays that offer real upgrades instead of
  a life top-up.
- **Game designer** — wants the supply dial in **one** shared place (`GameRules` /
  level-scaling curves) and no leftover Extra Life sources, so re-tuning needs one
  edit and no scene diverge.
- **Maintainer** — wants the reward pools to be honest: no dead Extra Life offer
  path, and docs/tests that match shipped numbers.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want at most half as many power-ups per kill as today, so each
  pickup feels earned.
- As a **player**, I want destroying asteroids to stop handing out extra lives, so
  lives come from deliberate play rather than rock-grinding.
- As a **player**, I want the hold-full and mini-boss rewards to offer upgrades
  rather than a life top-up, so the reward moment is about building the ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-kill drop rate halved:** `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_LEVEL_1`
  is `0.09` (was `0.18`) and `DEFAULT_POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE_AT_MAX_LEVEL` is `0.025`
  (was `0.05`), so `powerUpDropChance(level)` from `src/core/levelScaling.ts` is
  half its former value at **every** level of the 1–10 campaign while keeping the
  linear ramp (L10 stays ≈ 27.8 % of L1). The re-exported
  `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE` (documented level-1 base) becomes `0.09`. Verified by unit
  tests on the defaults and on the curve endpoints plus an intermediate level.
- [ ] **AC2 — No double-halving of Extra Life's share:** `DEFAULT_EXTRA_LIFE_WEIGHT`
  stays `3` and no other drop weight changes, so Extra Life's *relative* rarity in
  the shared pool (≈ 5.2 % of power-up draws) is untouched — only the per-kill roll
  falls. Its absolute per-kill chance at L1 drops from ≈ 0.93 % to ≈ 0.47 %.
  Verified by a rules/spawner-share test.
- [ ] **AC3 — Asteroids stop dropping Extra Life:** `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance`
  defaults to `0` (was `0.05`); the shared rule (`rollAsteroidExtraLife`), the
  `GameRules` key and its clamping/persistence stay in place so a designer can
  re-enable it. At the default, a fully destroyed small asteroid never spawns an
  `extra_life` pickup in `PlayScene` or in any asteroid-bearing gym. Verified by
  unit tests on the default and by a seeded kill-path test at the default chance.
- [ ] **AC4 — Extra Life removed from every reward surface:** `extra_life` is
  excluded from the hold-full choice pool (`CHOICE_POOL`), from owned
  `power-up-level`/`power-up-charge` offers and from the mini-boss reward wheel
  (wedges and the empty-owned "hold-full-style" fallback). It remains a
  **field-pickup-only** power-up: still spawned by the shared drop pool, still
  granted +1 life on collection, and still levelled by field pickups. Verified by
  tests showing no `extra_life` option in hold-full draws (over many seeded draws),
  no `extra_life` wedge for a run that owns it, and the fallback pool excluding it.
  The now-unreachable demo-bot hold-full preference for Extra Life
  (`_preferredDemoChoiceIndex`) is removed or simplified with its assertions and docs
  — no dead offer path is left behind.
- [ ] **AC5 — Persisted configs adopt the new defaults:** `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  rises to `5`, and `loadRules` resets `powerUpDropChanceAtLevel1`,
  `powerUpDropChanceAtMaxLevel` and `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` to the new
  defaults for any config older than version 5 (same precedent as the v2/v3
  migrations), because `saveRules` persists the whole blob and a stored
  `0.18`/`0.05` would silently defeat the change at runtime. Blobs explicitly
  stamped version 5 keep their tuned values.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation:** unit tests cover the new defaults, the migration,
  the asteroid default-off path and the reward-surface exclusions; the existing
  repo-wide guards (`src/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`)
  are updated where the exclusion is deliberate, not weakened.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **One shared source of truth:** all tuning lives in `src/core/rules.ts` /
  `src/core/levelScaling.ts`; no scene, gym or test may hard-code the new numbers.
- **Gym↔game parity** (`docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): the game and
  every gym must run the same code. All four surfaces already live in shared modules,
  so the change must be made there, not per scene.
- **Do not delete the asteroid rule** (operator decision Q2): keep it configurable
  with a zero default.
- Extra Life's rarity *weight*, the 5-life cap, the `lifeGain` level curve and the
  catalogue entry are unchanged.

## Existing state

Three independent sources and two reward surfaces produce Extra Life today:

1. **Per-kill shared drop pool** — `PlayScene._maybeDropPowerUp` rolls
   `powerUpDropChance(level, rules)` (linear `0.18` at L1 → `0.05` at L10,
   AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X) and draws from the shared `WeightedRandomSpawner`
   (weights: 12 standard IDs × 4, Mystery UFO 3, **Extra Life 3**, Smart Bomb 2,
   Orbital Strike 2 → pool total 58 → Extra Life ≈ 5.2 % of power-up draws; the
   weight was raised 1 → 3 by AH-0MUNS3VAQ0023L1J).
2. **Small-asteroid roll** — `rollAsteroidExtraLife` (`src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts`,
   AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S) adds an independent `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` roll
   (default `0.05`, scaled by the level drop-chance ratio) on every fully destroyed
   small asteroid, additive to the generic pool. Consumed by `PlayScene`,
   `GymFormationScene` (incl. `GymMinerals`) and `GymLevel`.
3. **Hold-full choice** — `CHOICE_POOL` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) lists
   `extra_life` as a base entry (weight 1.0×), and `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`
   offers a `power-up-level` (lifeGain 1 → 3) once Extra Life is owned. Gyms
   consume the same builder (`GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymWeaponLeveling`).
4. **Mini-boss reward wheel** — `openMiniBossReward` builds wedges from
   `resolvePlayerSlotState(player).ownedIds` (`buildWheelWedges`), so a run that
   permanently holds Extra Life gets an Extra Life wedge; when nothing is owned the
   reward falls back to the same three-option hold-full choice
   (`_holdFullStyleRewardOptions`).

Related runtime code: the demo bot prefers an offered Extra Life in the hold-full
auto-select (`PlayScene._preferredDemoChoiceIndex`, AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4) — that
preference becomes unreachable once Extra Life leaves the pool. `saveRules` is
called by the gym interval slider (`src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts`) with the whole
`GameRules` blob, so stored configs can carry the current chance values.

Docs carrying the current numbers: GDD §4.4 (pool weights, the 0.18 → 0.05 curve,
the asteroid 0.05 roll, the `availableWhenSlotsFull` choice behaviour), GDD §3
difficulty summary, `docs/BALANCING.md` scaling table, `README.md` (rules config
and `asteroidKillDrops` entries), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
(asteroid drop), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` (`GymMinerals` row).

## Desired change

- Halve the per-kill power-up drop chance curve: L1 `0.18 → 0.09`, L10
  `0.05 → 0.025`, ramp shape preserved.
- Leave every drop weight (including Extra Life's `3`) untouched.
- Default the asteroid Extra Life roll to `0`, keeping the rule and config key.
- Exclude `extra_life` from the hold-full choice pool, its owned level-up offers and
  the mini-boss wheel/fallback — one shared, documented exclusion so the game and
  every gym drop it together; Extra Life stays a field pickup.
- Retire the now-unreachable demo-bot hold-full preference for Extra Life (and its
  tests/docs), noting that on-screen Extra Life pursuit stays (field pickups still
  exist).
- Bump the rules schema to 5 so stored configs adopt the new defaults.
- Update the docs and tests that pin the old numbers.

## Key Files

- `src/core/rules.ts` — new drop-chance and asteroid-chance defaults;
  `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5` plus the v5 migration branch in `loadRules`.
- `src/core/levelScaling.ts` — doc comments and the `POWER_UP_DROP_CHANCE`
  re-export (no formula change).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — documented `extra_life` exclusion for the choice pool
  and the owned level-up offer builder (`buildChoiceCandidates`,
  `buildOwnedPowerUpOffer`/`buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`).
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` — exclude `extra_life` from `buildWheelWedges`
  (and from the outcome pool) for owned kinds.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_holdFullStyleRewardOptions` /
  `openMiniBossReward` fallback follow the shared exclusion;
  `_preferredDemoChoiceIndex` dead preference retired.
- `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.ts` — comment only (rule retained, default 0).
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — only if the `availableWhenSlotsFull` wording needs a
  note (Extra Life still slot-exempt for pickups).
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`, `src/core/levelScaling.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/asteroidKillDrops.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts`, `src/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/MiniBossWheelScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` — assertions
  and stored-rule blobs (which must be stamped `version: 5` to opt out of the migration).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 (pool weights, drop curve, asteroid roll,
  `availableWhenSlotsFull` wording), §3 difficulty summary, Extra Life catalogue row.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — scaling table and rationale (per-kill chance column, asteroid
  Extra Life column now 0).
- `README.md` — rules-config and `asteroidKillDrops` descriptions; hold-full
  choice/mini-boss reward descriptions.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — asteroid Extra
  Life and `GymMinerals` row wording.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUNS3VAQ0023L1J** — Increase the probability of lives powerup being spawned
  (completed): raised the Extra Life **weight** 1 → 3, which this item deliberately
  leaves alone (the supply reduction comes from the per-kill chance instead).
- **AH-0MV6M2M9P0078N4S** — Asteroids drop more lives (completed): introduced the
  asteroid Extra Life roll this item defaults to off (rule retained).
- **AH-0MVLJF5P0005KF8X** — Use level-resolved power-up drop chance in PlayScene
  (completed): owns the `powerUpDropChance` curve whose defaults this item halves.
- **AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P** — level-scaling parent (completed): the tuning contract
  for the 1→2× counts / 0.18→0.05 drop chance axes.
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** — Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice and
  on-screen pickups (completed): its hold-full preference is retired here; the
  on-screen pursuit stays.
- **AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD** / **AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON** — mini-boss reward wheel and the
  shared level-up offer seam whose surface this item narrows.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4, `docs/BALANCING.md`,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the documentation being brought back in line.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** – Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice and on-screen pickups (completed)
- **AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55** – Post-MVP Hangar War: special missions with special rewards (open)
- **AH-0MVSAJVHF007QO6V** – Terminal reward and destruction feedback (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: boss, dropping, extra, far, full (+18 more)
- `README.md` — matched: boss, dropping, extra, far, full (+17 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: boss, dropping, extra, far, full (+16 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Whole-supply reduction (accepted trade-off):** operator answer Q1 = (b) halves
  the **per-kill drop chance for every power-up**, not just Extra Life, so all
  upgrades land less often. Weapon drops from the pool fall by the same half — this
  is the intended reading of "half them from ship".
- **Assumption — both curve endpoints halve** (0.18 → 0.09 and 0.05 → 0.025) so the
  ramp shape and the "L10 ≈ 30 % of L1" property survive; halving only the L1 value
  would flatten the curve and over-supply late levels.
- **Migration risk:** the v5 reset applies to any blob *without* a v5 stamp — the
  two gym tests that force `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance: 1` must therefore write
  `version: RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION`, otherwise the migration zeroes their fixture.
- **Parity-test intent:** `choicePool.parity.test.ts` asserts pool ≡ catalogue −
  `reset`; the Extra Life exclusion must be added **explicitly** in that test (as a
  deliberate exclusion) so the guard keeps catching genuinely missing entries.
- **Balance assumption:** the halved rate and the zeroed asteroid roll are the
  operator's chosen values; if playtesting shows over-correction, re-tune the
  `GameRules` defaults in a separate item.
- **Dead-code risk:** removing Extra Life from the choice pool strands the demo
  bot's `_preferredDemoChoiceIndex` branch; delete or simplify it and its assertions
  rather than leaving an unreachable path + stale docs.
- **Docs-assertion tests:** several tests pin documentation wording rather than
  behaviour (`src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts`, `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts`,
  plus the GDD/BALANCING assertions); budget for updating them with the docs.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do **not** change Extra Life's weight, the 5-life cap, the
  `lifeGain` level curve, other drop weights, the Mystery UFO treatment, or the
  threat-free `GymPowerUpsUtility` round-robin gallery (it deliberately cycles Extra
  Life as a demo). Record extra opportunities as linked work items instead.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should "half them from ship" be implemented?** (a) Halve the Extra Life
  *weight* in the shared drop pool (3 → 1.5; ≈ 5.2 % → ≈ 2.7 % of power-up draws),
  (b) halve the ship's *overall per-kill drop chance* (halves all power-up drops),
  (c) other. — **Answer (operator): "(b)"** — halve the overall per-kill drop
  chance, and **update the work item title and description** to match. Source:
  interactive reply (round 1), 2026-11-04. The title was therefore changed to
  "Halve per-kill power-up drops and remove Extra Life from reward screens".
- **Q2: "Stop asteroids dropping them" — remove the rule, or disable it?** (a) Remove
  `rollAsteroidExtraLife` and the `asteroidExtraLifeDropChance` key entirely,
  (b) keep the rule and set the default chance to `0`. — **Answer (operator):
  "(2) b"** — keep the shared rule/config key, default the chance to `0`. Source:
  interactive reply (round 1), 2026-11-04.
- **Q3: Which reward surfaces should exclude Extra Life?** (a) All of them — hold-full
  choice pool, its owned level-up offers, the mini-boss wheel and the empty-owned
  fallback (Extra Life becomes field-pickup-only), (b) mini-boss wheel only,
  (c) keep everywhere at reduced weight. — **Answer (operator): "(3) a"** — every
  reward surface excludes Extra Life; field pickups still grant lives. Source:
  interactive reply (round 1), 2026-11-04.

### Agent decisions recorded during intake (not operator-answered)

- **Both curve endpoints halve** (`0.18 → 0.09`, `0.05 → 0.025`): derived from Q1(b) —
  halving the rate "at runtime" means the whole campaign curve, not only level 1.
- **Rules schema bump to 5** for the three affected keys: without it,
  `saveRules`-written blobs (whole-blob writes from the gym slider) keep the old
  `0.18`/`0.05` values and the halving would not take effect at runtime. Precedent:
  the v2 and v3 migrations reset tunables whose stored values became meaningless.
- **`GymPowerUpsUtility` keeps its round-robin Extra Life cycle**: it is a
  threat-free demonstration gallery (documented gym-only divergence), not a gameplay
  reward surface.

# Model player weapon fire output in the balance harness

discovered-from:AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T (found while running the measured gate
AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL).

## Problem

The Q3 = B measured gate for the weapon nerf (**Weapon upgrades are too
powerful** (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T)) **cannot see a weapon-output change**. The
closed-loop headless arena fires the player's shots on a fixed cadence
constant:

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` → `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS = 9`,
  `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 420`, `PLAYER_BULLET_LIFETIME = 0.75` — one bullet
  every 9 ticks regardless of the equipped weapon;
- the only import from `src/utils/weapons` in the whole `src/ai/eval/` tree
  is `import type { WeaponId }` — a **type-only** import, erased at compile
  time, so `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `AOE_RADII`,
  hit budgets and `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` can never reach the simulation.

Measured, not inferred: the post-change 100-game campaign batch is
**byte-identical** to the pre-change baseline (every per-run `recordsHash`
included), and a sensitivity probe that temporarily raised
`DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS.cannon` from 2 to 12 (six times the starting
weapon's cadence) also produced a byte-identical 3-game report. Evidence:
`docs/BALANCING.md` §"Weapon 40 % trim / flattened curve — measured
before/after gate".

## Why it matters

- Every future weapon damage/output tuning item that relies on the batch gate
  gets a guaranteed zero delta and a misleading "no effect" reading.
- The intended-experience bands (`src/data/experience-targets.json`) can never
  detect a weapon-output regression, because the metric input does not depend
  on weapon data.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary already documents the limitation
  ("the arena's auto-fire is fixed"); this item closes it deliberately rather
  than leaving it implicit.

## Goal (user story)

*As the balancing agent, I want the headless arena to fire with the equipped
weapons and their level-resolved statistics, so a weapon damage, cadence or
pattern change moves the batch metrics and the measured gate can actually
answer the question it was created for.*

## Suggested approach

1. Replace the fixed auto-fire with the shared weapon resolution: use
   `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolveWeaponPattern` from
   `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` plus `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` /
   `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` / `AOE_RADII` from
   `src/utils/weapons.ts`; spawn per-weapon projectiles (pattern count,
   offsets, lifetime, size, pierce budget, bounce, AOE radius) rather than one
   bullet down the facing vector.
2. Resolve the arena's weapon levels from the same ownership context the
   hold-full choice flow already maintains
   (`ChoiceContext.weaponLevels`), so a chosen `weapon-level` upgrade rung
   changes the arena's output exactly as it does in `Player`.
3. Keep the change inside the shared code (gym↔game parity rule,
   AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): no arena-local copy of a weapon constant.
4. Re-record a baseline: the metrics will move by design, so
   `src/data/experience-targets.json` must be re-baselined
   (`targetsVersion` bump) with GDD §2.7 updated in the **same** change.
5. Re-run the weapon-trim gate evidence
   (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T / AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL) afterwards, so the 40 % trim
   finally has a measured before/after.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The arena's player projectiles are spawned from the resolved equipped
  weapon(s) (pattern count, offsets, cadence, lifetime) rather than a fixed
  `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS` bullet, asserting that a level-resolved weapon change
  changes the arena's damage output.
- [ ] A sensitivity test proves the harness now **sees** a weapon-output change:
  the same-seed batch differs when a weapon's cadence, pattern count or AOE
  radius changes (the inverse of the AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL probe).
- [ ] Weapon levels resolved from the run's ownership context feed the arena's
  fire output, so a `weapon-level` choice is observable in the metrics.
- [ ] No duplicated weapon constant or resolver exists in `src/ai/eval/`; the
  arena consumes `src/utils/weapons.ts` / `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`.
- [ ] `src/data/experience-targets.json` is re-baselined (`targetsVersion`
  bumped) and GDD §2.7 updated in the same change.
- [ ] `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary and the weapon-trim evidence
  section are updated to state that weapon output **is** modelled.
- [ ] The full project test suite passes.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the fixed auto-fire and projectile model.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — the catalogue,
  cadence, pattern and level resolvers to consume.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — the arena behaviour and determinism tests.
- `src/data/experience-targets.json`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.7 —
  the re-baseline and narrative.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the fidelity boundary and the before/after evidence.

## Notes

- Scope note: this is deliberately **not** part of the weapon-trim epic (AC4
  scope guard) — it is a harness capability gap, not a balance change.
- Do not retune any weapon value in this item; it only makes the instrument
  capable of measuring them.

## Goal

Remove the measured #1 frame-time hotspot at 100 late-game enemies: every bullet is its own Phaser \`Graphics\` object, re-batched and re-submitted every frame.

**User story:** As a desktop player, I want late-game bullet load to stop costing ~10 % of the frame in draw submission, so 100 enemies plus their fire can hold 60 FPS.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

Profile of \`GymPerformance\` (100 enemies, ~200-345 live enemy bullets), 60 s, desktop headless Chromium, commit 3e33e5c9:

- Phaser \`GraphicsWebGLRenderer\` 4.18 % of the measured window (28.3 % of JS), \`batch\` 2.97 % (20.1 % of JS), Graphics pipeline \`run\` x3 ~2.82 % (19.2 % of JS) — **~10 % of the window / ~68 % of JS**, and it drives most of the 84.75 % \`native\` GL submission time.
- Animated pellets redraw their \`Graphics\` every frame, so earcut re-triangulates the path per frame: \`earcutLinked\` 0.49 %, \`linkedList\` 0.21 % of the window.
- Cost scales with live bullets, not enemies: the gym (~200 bullets) sits at p50 33.3 ms; \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (mean 269 enemies, ~33 bullets) sits at p50 16.7 ms.
- Baseline and full ranking: \`docs/PERFORMANCE.md\` (Baseline, Ranked hotspots).

## Scope

- Replace the per-bullet \`Graphics\` object with a cached texture/sprite per bullet shape (shape + colour + rim + tail), so a bullet is one sprite in a batched draw rather than a Graphics object with its own pipeline.
- Animate the pulsing pellet with sprite scale/alpha instead of a per-frame \`drawBulletShape\` redraw.
- Keep the visual result equivalent (shape, colour, rim, tail, pulse) and keep it in the shared seam (\`src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts\`, \`src/entities/bulletUtils.ts\`) so gyms and \`PlayScene\` run the same code (AGENTS.md gym/game parity).
- No gameplay, balance or determinism change: bullet positions, speeds, collisions and RNG consumption are untouched.

## Out of scope

- Collision broad-phase and allocation work (separate children, measured too small to matter).
- HUD/bubble/pod Graphics redraws (AH-0MVXV0FFJ0066EC8 keeps that scope).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A bullet of every shape is rendered from a cached texture/sprite; no per-bullet \`scene.add.graphics()\` remains on the bullet path (verified by a test on the shared seam and by the profiler).
2. The pulsing pellet animates without a per-frame \`drawBulletShape\` redraw.
3. \`GymPerformance\` at 100 enemies, 60 s, same host and load band as the baseline: p50 and p95 frame time improve by >= 20 % vs the recorded baseline in \`docs/PERFORMANCE.md\`, with before/after numbers and a profile attached to the work item.
4. Parity and determinism preserved: gym/game equivalence tests and seeded bot determinism pass.
5. Full project test suite passes; \`docs/PERFORMANCE.md\` records the before/after numbers.

**Measured, fixed, and re-measured (chrome scope).**

## What the profile actually said

The epic profile (AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5) ranked HUD/bubble/pod/timer-bar chrome at 0.02–0.03 % of the window because the `GymPerformance` stress gym holds **no power-ups** — so the baseline never rendered a single HUD loadout row. The per-bullet `Graphics` object (≈10 % of the window) is real and is owned by AH-0MW2DAY2L004QSKF; this item's own scope had to be measured separately, not read off that ranking.

## Measurement (ablation, same scene, same host)

`GymPowerUpsCombat`, 30 s window / 5 s warm-up, `--profile`, headless Chromium (SwiftShader):

- **plain** — `--setup '{"threatCount":12}'`
- **armed** — same scene plus a scripted loadout: `--setup '{"powerUps":{"shield":1,"force_field":1,"thorns":1,"magnet":1,"bomb":1},"player":{"weapons":["options"]},"threatCount":12}'` (five HUD rows + Shield/Force Field/Thorns bubbles + Options escort)

| Run | Host load | JS (% window) | `ui` | `gc` | FPS | p95 (ms) | Frames > 33 ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain, before | 5.64 | 5.05 | 0.02 | 0.18 | 58.8 | 16.8 | 36 |
| plain, after | 8.88 | 4.96 | 0.08 | 0.22 | 57.5 | 16.8 | 76 |
| armed, before | 7.14 | **9.06** | 0.13 | 0.39 | 51.3 | 33.4 | 261 |
| armed, after (run A) | 13.49 | **5.44** | 0.08 | 0.18 | 53.2 | 33.3 | 200 |
| armed, after (run B, final code) | 10.26 | **5.79** | 0.14 | 0.21 | 49.8 | 33.4 | 306 |

FPS/percentiles on this shared host are noise-dominated (other agents' suites were running); the JS attribution is the stable signal. Every Phaser text-path symbol that appears only when rows exist disappears after the change (self time, % of window, armed before): `texImage2D` 0.99, `save` 0.49, `preDestroy` 0.47, `updateText` 0.39, `MeasureText` 0.27, `setStyle` 0.27, `Text` 0.25, `create` 0.25, `measureText` 0.20, `fillText` 0.19 — all below the top-16 cut (each < 0.15 %) afterwards. The armed run now sits within noise of the plain run despite a higher load average, so the HUD rows are effectively free.

**Not material / not changed:** the Shield, Force Field and Thorns bubbles, the Options escort and the wave-timer bar are each a single `Graphics` whose geometry either moves every frame (orbiting pods, depleting timer fill) or is cheaper to redraw than to diff. `GraphicsWebGLRenderer` measures 1.12 % armed vs 1.07 % plain, i.e. inside the noise floor, which corroborates the epic ranking: the measured draw-submission cost is the per-bullet `Graphics` object, not the chrome. Converting them to cached textures would trade a measurable-zero draw cost for a visual-parity risk, so they are deliberately untouched.

**Target load:** a 60 s `GymPerformance` re-run after the change (100 enemies, 326 enemy-bullet peak, load 15.71) reproduced the documented high-load baseline rows 4–5 exactly — 26.81 FPS vs 26.77/26.80, p50 33.4 ms, p95 50.0 vs 50.1 ms — confirming no regression at the target load (that scenario renders no HUD rows).

## What changed

`src/ui/HUD.ts` (shared by `PlayScene` and every combat gym, gym↔game parity):

1. `refresh()` now resolves a **render plan** (rows, indices, labels, values, greyed/marker state, lives label, layout inputs) and rebuilds the row `GameObject`s only when that plan differs from what is on screen. Previously every frame destroyed and re-created a `Graphics` icon plus two `Text` objects per row, each regenerating a canvas texture and re-uploading it — for state that changes at most once a second (countdowns are whole seconds).
2. The row **model** arrays (`_rows`/`_weaponRows`, read by `getRows()`/`getLoadoutRows()`) are still refreshed every frame, so no consumer sees a stale value just because the rendered text is unchanged.
3. The mineral hold bar redraws only when its geometry (fill width / visibility) changes.

## Canvas fallback (AC5)

No `RenderTexture`, no canvas readback, no WebGL-only API is introduced — the change only decides *when* existing `Text`/`Graphics` objects are created, and both are renderer-agnostic Phaser objects. The unit/integration harness boots a real `Phaser.Game` with `type: Phaser.AUTO` in happy-dom where only a Canvas 2D context exists (`src/test/setup.ts`), so the new `src/ui/HUD.refreshCadence.test.ts` exercises the optimised path on the Canvas renderer.

## Tests

`src/ui/HUD.refreshCadence.test.ts` (7 tests) pins both halves of the contract: rendered rows are the **same objects** across a refresh whose state did not change; every visible change still reaches the screen on the next refresh (countdown tick, new pickup, lives change, mineral-bar layout shift); the mineral bar clears only when its geometry moves; and 120 unchanged frames do not accumulate row objects. Full suite: 446 files / 10 004 tests green (run through the test skill).
